---
title: "Lucifer's Declared Plan"
slug: lucifers-declared-plan
order: 30
permalink: /books/meat-bibles-symbolic-language/lucifers-declared-plan/
description: "Isaiah's five declarations are one act heard twice: the son of darkness will make himself like the Most High by raising his covered lunar seat into the sun's apparent place, bringing the Highest Light to silence for himself and corrupting the sign that governs God's appointed times."
og_title: "Lucifer's Declared Plan — MEAT The Bible's Symbolic Language"
epigraphs:
  - quote: "For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne above the stars of God."
    ref: "Isaiah 14:13"
---
The plan was never announced.
It was __“said in thine heart,”__ where no creature could hear it; but the LORD is He who __“declareth unto man what is his thought”__ (Amos 4:13).
God read the counsel where it was conceived and commanded His people to take it up as a proverb against the king of Babylon (Isaiah 14:4).
The conspirator kept his counsel; the Judge published it.

[quote.scripture, Isaiah 14:12-15]
____
How art thou fallen from heaven, O *Lucifer, son of the morning*! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst *weaken the nations*!
For thou hast said in thine heart, I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my *throne* above the sym:sym-stars[*stars of God*]: I will sit also upon the sym:sym-mountain[*mount*] *of the congregation*, in the *sides of the north*:
I will ascend above the *heights of the clouds*; I will *be like the most High*.
Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the *sides of the pit*.
____

The received reading is true: the rebel intends to make himself like the Most High.
Nothing that follows asks that reading to yield its place.
The question is whether it says all that the words say.
It tells us his ambition, but leaves the strange precision of the boast unresolved.
Why a mountain of assembly?
Why the recesses of the north?
Why do stars, high places, and a dark cloud carry an ambition usually reduced to an abstract wish to be God?

The consonants answer in stages: first their permitted senses, then the second reading beneath __“throne,”__ then the double reading at the summit.
Only after the words stand do the symbols enter.

[discrete]
=== First Hearing: The Darkness in the Words

The name opens with a contradiction.
_Helel_ is the shining one, yet the consonants under _shachar_ serve both the noun *dawn* and the verb *be black* — the verb Job uses when __“my skin is *black* upon me”__ (Job 30:30).
_Ben_, son, names more than physical descent: the sons of Belial are characterized by worthlessness, and the children of light are characterized by sym:sym-light[light].
The phrase is therefore heard twice: *son of dawn* and *son — the product and bearer — of blackness*.footnote:shachar[The second is a same-consonant wordplay, not a claim that the noun *dawn* is grammatically impossible: H7837 is the noun _shachar_, dawn; H7835 is the verb _shachar_, be black. The son-language supplies the characterization.]
He appears bright but produces darkness.

The same darkness gathers around his destination.
The King James’ __“mount of the congregation”__ is _har moed_.
_Moed_ does mean an assembly, but its full lexical field is *appointed time, appointed place, and appointed meeting*.
The Torah refuses to separate those senses: __“the appointed times (_moedim_) of the LORD”__ are the days Israel must __“proclaim to be holy convocations”__ (Leviticus 23:2).
_Har moed_ is the mountain — the high place — of the appointed assembly.

The __“sides of the north”__ are _yarkete tsaphon_.
_Yarkete_ means the farthest or innermost recesses: the hold of Jonah's ship, the recess of David's cave, and, in the sentence answering this boast, the recesses of the pit (Jonah 1:5; 1 Samuel 24:3; Isaiah 14:15).
The points read the final word _tsaphon_, north; the same consonants read _tsafun_, *hidden, concealed, treasured*.
Scripture uses that second form for Jerusalem, God's treasured place, and for His saints, __“thy hidden ones”__ (Ezekiel 7:22; Psalm 83:3).
The phrase can therefore be heard as *the innermost recesses of the hidden place*.

The north reading remains true and supplies another witness.
Psalm 48 uses Isaiah's exact phrase for Zion: __“mount Zion, in the *recesses of the north*, the city of the great King”__ (Psalm 48:2).
The north is not an idle compass direction; it is the royal mountain of God's presence.
He seeks the hidden seat of the King and the appointed assembly gathered there.
Hiddenness also keeps the darkness already present in the name: Job says __“all darkness shall be hidden in his secret places,”__ using this same root (Job 20:26).

The next word makes the darkness visible.
The __“cloud”__ is _av_, a *dark cloud* or cloud-mass, and what he ascends upon is its _bamah_ — its height or high place.
The immediate vocabulary has now supplied a shining one who bears blackness, a mountain of appointed meeting, an innermost hidden place, and the high place of a dark cloud.
No symbol has created that pattern; the words have.

[quote.scripture, Isaiah 14:12-14 — first hearing from the consonants]
____
How art thou fallen from heaven, *shining one, son and bearer of blackness*!
For thou hast said in thine heart: I will ascend the heavens; I will raise my *seat* above the stars of God; I will sit in the *high place of the appointed assembly*, in the *innermost recesses of the hidden place*;
I will ascend upon the *high places of the dark cloud*; I will make myself like the Highest.
____

The seat supplies the next hearing without yet importing a sun, calendar, or eclipse.

[discrete]
=== Second Hearing: The Full Moon and the Covered Seat

__“I will exalt my *throne*.”__
The pointed word is _kisse'_ — a throne, a royal seat, the place from which its owner rules.
Strong's traces it to covering: a covered or canopied seat.
Strip the possessive ending from __“my throne,”__ and the letters are כסא — the same letters that spell _keseh_, the *full moon*.

This is not a spelling assembled for Isaiah.
Proverbs writes the full-moon word exactly that way, כסא: __“he will come home at the *full moon*”__ (Proverbs 7:20, ASV).
Psalm 81 uses its other biblical spelling, כסה, in the command to sound the trumpet __“at the *full moon*, on our solemn feast day”__ (Psalm 81:3, NKJV).
The throne has the same two spellings, כסא and כסה.
Point the letters one way and the seat is a throne; point them another and the seat is the moon at fulness.

Job writes the throne with the second spelling and then covers its face:

[quote.scripture, Job 26:9, ASV]
____
He incloseth the face of his *throne*, and spreadeth his cloud upon it.
____

Read _kisseh_, and a throne is veiled by cloud.
Read _keseh_, and the full moon's face is veiled by cloud.
The sentence survives either hearing, and the psalm of David removes any doubt that throne and luminary belong together:

[quote.scripture, Psalm 89:36-37]
____
His seed shall endure for ever, and his *throne as the* sym:sym-sun[sun] before me.
It shall be established for ever *as the* sym:sym-moon[moon], and as a sym:sym-faithful-witness[faithful witness] in heaven.
____

The throne is set as the sun and established as the moon before any wordplay is asked to carry the identification.
The consonants then bind the throne specifically to lunar fulness.
Isaiah's __“my throne”__ can therefore be heard as *my covered seat* and as *my full-moon seat* — a claimed place among the lights.

The surrounding words decide how his version is covered.
The LORD __“coverest thyself with *light* as with a garment”__ (Psalm 104:2); the faithful witness bears the whole face of the sun through the night.
Lucifer is the son of blackness, operating from the hidden place beneath a dark cloud.
He claims the throne of fulness and covers it in the opposite substance.
His is not the faithful full moon shining from the Father's light; it is the lunar seat covered in darkness.

[quote.scripture, Isaiah 14:13 — the seat heard twice]
____
I will raise *my covered lunar seat* above the stars of God; I will sit in the high place of the appointed assembly, in the innermost recesses of the hidden place.
____

[discrete]
=== Third Hearing: The Highest Light Silenced

_Elyon_ is both an adjective and a title.
As an adjective it means *high, upper, uppermost*; as a title it names God, *the Most High*.
Isaiah has filled the sentence with the heavens, stars, a lunar seat, height, and cloud.
Inside that field, the unnamed uppermost light is the sun — __“the greater light to rule the day”__ (Genesis 1:16) — and the title and the symbol meet in one verse: __“the LORD God is a sun”__ (Psalm 84:11).
The Most High and the Highest Light are not rival referents.
One is the Person; the other is His sign.

The verb before _elyon_ is likewise heard twice.
The consonants of _edameh_ belong to two verbs kept side by side in the lexicon.
The first means *be like, resemble*: __“I will make myself like the Most High.”__
The second means *cease, cause to cease, cut off, destroy* — the verb Isaiah uses when Moab is __“brought to silence”__ and Hosea when a mother is destroyed (Isaiah 15:1; Hosea 4:5).

The form is Hithpael, whose self-reference need not make the subject the thing silenced.
The stem can describe an action done *for oneself, in one's own interest*, while taking an external object; Biblical Hebrew can also mark an affected object with _le_, the letter _lamed_ attached here to _elyon_.footnote:hithpael[The _tav_ of the Hithpael prefix regularly assimilates before a root-initial _dalet_; without points, the resulting form is written with the same letters as Isaiah's _edameh_. The stem can express action performed “for oneself” and can take an external object (Gesenius, _Hebrew Grammar_, §§54.2-3, 117w). Scripture also marks destructive targets with _le_: Joab and Abishai __“slew Abner”__ (2 Samuel 3:30), Israel would __“destroy all this people”__ (Numbers 32:15), and Saul sought __“to destroy the city”__ (1 Samuel 23:10; §117n). Scripture preserves no second Hithpael occurrence of the silence-root; this reading rests on the regular productive formation and the independently attested transitive sense “cause to cease,” not on a duplicate of Isaiah's form.]
The alternate hearing is therefore not *I will silence myself* but *I will bring the Highest to silence for myself*.

[quote.scripture, Isaiah 14:14 — spoken once, heard twice]
____
I will ascend upon the high places of the dark cloud;
I will *make myself like the Highest* —
I will *bring the Highest to silence for myself*.
____

The readings are not rivals.
The received reading states his ambition: make himself like the Most High.
The second hearing adds the act by which he pursues it: bring the Highest Light to silence by taking its place.
Together they disclose the whole: *I will make myself like the Most High by taking His place, and I will bring the Highest Light to silence for myself by covering it.*

[discrete]
=== The Symbols Take Their Places

The words have earned their readings; Scripture now supplies the identities.

The sym:sym-stars[stars] are the righteous: __“they that turn many to righteousness”__ shine __“as the stars for ever and ever”__ (Daniel 12:3).
A sym:sym-mountain[mountain] is a kingdom: Daniel's stone becomes a great mountain filling the earth, and Daniel interprets it as the kingdom God establishes over every other kingdom (Daniel 2:35, 44).
The mountain of the appointed assembly is therefore the kingdom of God's covenant people gathered at His appointed times.

The moon governs when that assembly meets.
The lights were given __“for signs, and for seasons”__ — _moedim_ — from the fourth day, and __“he appointed the moon for seasons”__ (Genesis 1:14; Psalm 104:19).
Leviticus joins the time to the people: the _moedim_ are appointed days proclaimed as holy convocations.
To seize the lunar throne is to seize the signal by which the stars of God assemble.

The hidden recess now joins both people and place.
Psalm 48 locates the city of the great King in the _yarkete tsaphon_; Psalm 83 calls God's people His _tsafunim_, His hidden ones.
The rebel seeks the hidden royal seat of the appointed assembly, and he operates its lunar sign from the phase hidden from sight.
The legitimate throne is the full moon, standing opposite the sun and carrying its whole face through the night.
The counterfeit takes that office to the opposite station: the moon covered in darkness, beside the sun, reflecting nothing toward the earth.
Isaiah pronounces woe upon precisely that exchange: __“that put darkness for light, and light for darkness”__ (Isaiah 5:20).

[discrete]
=== One Place, Two Readings

Every verb in the boast moves through space: *ascend; raise above; sit; enter the recesses; ascend upon the high places; reach the Highest*.
His throne is his seat — his claimed place of rule.
To __“make myself like the Highest”__ inside this spatial sequence is not merely to imitate God's character; it is to put his seat where the sign of the Highest appears.

The sky performs the sentence exactly.
A full moon stands opposite the sun and can never cover it.
A moon covered in darkness stands on the sun's side of the earth; when the three bodies align, its black disk enters the sun's apparent position and covers the greater light.
It does not become the sun, generate the sun's light, or acquire the sun's authority.
It becomes *like* the sun by taking the sun's visible place.

Taking that place produces the second reading.
The heavens __“declare the glory of God,”__ and day pours forth speech from the tabernacle and circuit of the sun (Psalm 19:1-6).
Cover the sun and its visible testimony ceases; the counterfeit has brought the Highest Light to silence for itself.
Its likeness is substitution, and its substitution is suppression.

This is how Satan can appear as __“an angel of light”__ while producing darkness (2 Corinthians 11:14).
He does not create a greater light.
He raises a dark form into the light's position and depends upon the light he covers for every appearance of greatness.
The received reading names the usurpation; the second reading names the silencing by which it is attempted.

[quote.scripture, Isaiah 14:12-14 — read through the symbols]
____
How art thou fallen from heaven, *shining one, son of darkness*!
For thou hast said in thine heart: I will ascend the heavens; I will raise *my covered lunar throne* above the sym:sym-stars[*righteous of God*]; I will sit in the sym:sym-mountain[*kingdom of the appointed assembly*], in the *innermost hidden place*;
I will ascend beneath the *dark covering*; I will *make myself like the Highest by taking His place, and bring the Highest Light to silence for myself*.
____

[discrete]
=== The Appointed Times Corrupted

The eclipse explains why the plan passes through _har moed_: the moon marks the appointed meetings, and the stars are the people who keep them.
Raise the wrong moon above the stars and the people still count and assemble — but at the counterfeit's signal, a light that reflects nothing.

Daniel names the same agenda without the celestial figure.
The enemy __“shall wear out the saints of the most High, and think to change times and laws”__ (Daniel 7:25).
The saints and the times are attacked in one sentence because the times govern the saints’ assembly.
Isaiah gives the plan; Daniel gives its historical work: change the signal, change the assembly, and weaken the nations without requiring them to know whose calendar they follow.

The phase matters.
Begin the month with the full moon and the month's middle approaches the hidden conjunction; begin it with the hidden conjunction and the month's middle approaches the full moon.
The two reckonings invert the lights.
Only the covered conjunction can stand in the sun's apparent place and produce the sign Isaiah describes.
The counterfeit claims the full-moon throne while moving its rule to the phase that can cover the sun.

God answers the ambition in the rebel's own word.
He sought the _yarkete_ of the hidden royal place; the judgment brings him down to the _yarkete_ of the pit (Isaiah 14:15).
He asked for the highest recess and received the lowest.

[discrete]
=== The Sun Failed at Noon

The Prophets had already joined the sign to an appointed feast and an only son:

[quote.scripture, Amos 8:9-10]
____
And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the Lord GOD, that I will cause the sym:sym-sun[sun] to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the clear day:
And I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation… and I will make it as the mourning of an *only son*, and the end thereof as a bitter day.
____

The prophecy binds the pieces before the Gospels arrive: the sun fails at noon, an appointed feast becomes mourning, and the grief is the grief of an only son.
At the Passover cross, __“from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land unto the ninth hour”__ (Matthew 27:45).
Luke records the same sign in the vocabulary of cessation:

[quote.scripture, Luke 23:44-45, ASV]
____
And it was now about the sixth hour, and a darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour, the sun's light *failing*: and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst.
____

The sun failed, and the covering of the sanctuary was torn.
The sign lasted far beyond ordinary totality; Scripture does not reduce it to a natural eclipse.
It uses the eclipse's exact act: at the feast of the only Son, the greater light was covered at noon and its speech ceased over the land.

God had read the rebel's plan first and turned its image into testimony at the cross.
The darkness could not hold the Light; what looked like silencing became the heavens' loudest declaration.

The two readings of Isaiah therefore stand together.
__“I will make myself like the Most High”__ is the ambition to take His place.
__“I will bring the Highest to silence for myself”__ is the means: the covered lunar seat raised into the sun's position.
The stars, the appointed assembly, the hidden recess, the dark cloud, the Highest, and the answering recess of the pit all belong to that one act.

The counterfeit is precise because the original is precious.
The moon still marks the LORD's appointments, the full witness still bears the Father's light, and the next question is the price of recognizing that witness when it appears as one complete pearl in the night.

sources.content:
---
title: "The Pearls of Wisdom"
slug: the-pearl
order: 31
permalink: /books/meat-bibles-symbolic-language/the-pearl/
description: "The merchant is the Son who sells all to purchase His bride, not a sinner buying the kingdom. The adjoining treasure parable identifies the field as the world and God's people as His treasure; the pearl parable repeats the same Buyer. Proverbs prices Wisdom and the woman of valour above pearls, then paints the bride as the full moon: rising in the night, holding the circuit, distributing appointed portions, and shining with light her husband gives her. Revelation completes the picture in the Bride-city whose gates are each one pearl."
og_title: "The Pearls of Wisdom — MEAT The Bible's Symbolic Language"
epigraphs:
  - quote: "Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchant man, seeking goodly pearls: who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it."
    ref: "Matthew 13:45-46"
---
Jesus gives the pearl parable in one sentence:

[quote.scripture, Matthew 13:45-46]
____
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchant man, seeking *goodly pearls*: who, when he had found *one pearl of great price*, went and sold all that he had, and bought it.
____

The little parable turns on 2 questions: Who is the merchant, and what did he purchase?

The parable immediately before it tells of a man who sells all to buy a sym:sym-field[field] for the treasure hidden within it (Matthew 13:44).
The link:/books/symbolic-language/the-coin/[Coin] chapter has already followed those symbols: the field is the world, and the treasure within it is God's people — His peculiar treasure, refined as silver and gold (Matthew 13:38; Exodus 19:5; Job 23:10; Zechariah 13:9).
Within the same sequence, Jesus has identified the man sowing in that field as the Son of man (Matthew 13:37).
The next sentence repeats the purchase in a new form: a merchant finds one pearl, sells all, and buys it.
The buyer has not changed.
Proverbs 31 will bind both purchases into one woman's portrait: she is priced above sym:sym-pearl[pearls], is likened to the merchant's ships, calls her merchandise good, and buys the sym:sym-field[field].
The field and the pearl are not separate clues; Solomon gathers both parables around the same woman.

The Merchant is the Son, and the pearl is the bride He came to purchase.

[discrete]
=== The Bride in the Sky

Jesus begins by naming the realm: __“The kingdom of heaven is like”__ — literally, the kingdom of the heavens.
Genesis names the firmament *Heaven* and places the sym:sym-sun[sun], sym:sym-moon[moon], and sym:sym-stars[stars] within it (Genesis 1:8, 14-18).
Before the merchant takes a step, the parable has already lifted our eyes to the sky.

The link:/books/symbolic-language/sun-moon-and-stars/[Sun, Moon, and Stars] chapter established the relationships pictured there.
The sym:sym-sun[sun] represents the Father and the husband.
The sym:sym-moon[moon] is the sym:sym-faithful-witness[faithful witness]: the Son reflecting His Father, and the sym:sym-marriage[bride] reflecting her Bridegroom.
The moon represents the submissive side of a covenant relationship — the Son under His Father, and the bride under her husband (1 Corinthians 11:3; Ephesians 5:22-24).
It does not produce an independent light; it receives the light of its head and faithfully makes that light visible.

The parable asks us to find one complete pearl in that heavenly arrangement.
The full moon already answers in 2 ways: it has the visible shape of one complete pearl, and the moon represents the bride in the covenant relationship.
The next step is to follow the words of both purchases through Scripture: *field*, *treasure*, *buy*, *merchant*, *found*, *one*, *good*, *pearl*, *great price*, and *heaven*.

[discrete]
=== Following the Words

*Pearl* and *great price* lead directly to Proverbs.
First, sym:sym-wisdom[Wisdom] is priced above pearls:

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 3:15, KJV — “pearls” restored]
____
She is *more precious than* sym:sym-pearl[pearls]footnote:fn31peninim[Strong's H6443 defines _peninim_ as __“probably a pearl (as round).”__ The full lexical case—including the ancient translations and the difficult witness of Lamentations 4:7—is documented at TimeTested.Bible under __“Peninim: Why Pearl Fits Better Than Ruby.”__]: and all the things thou canst desire are not to be compared unto her.
____

Proverbs 8:11 and Job 28:18 repeat the comparison.
Then the woman of valour — the bride — is priced above the same pearls:

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:10 — MEAT rendering]
____
A woman of valour who can find? for her *price is far above* sym:sym-pearl[pearls]footnote:fn31peninim[].
____

The find-verb of Proverbs 3:13 returns in 2 revealing statements: __“whoso findeth *me*”__ (Proverbs 8:35, Wisdom speaking) and __“whoso findeth *a wife*”__ (Proverbs 18:22).
Wisdom and the bride occupy the same place in Solomon's search, and both lead back to the merchant's defining action: __“when he had *found* one pearl of great price”__ (Matthew 13:46).

*Merchant* and *good* converge there too.
Wisdom's __“merchandise”__ is good (Proverbs 3:14).
The bride __“tasteth that her merchandise is good”__ (Proverbs 31:18).
The kingdom's merchant seeks __“goodly pearls”__ (Matthew 13:45).
Wisdom, bride, pearl — the good merchandise is one continuous trail.

That leaves *one*.
If the trail is sound, Scripture should not merely compare a woman to a pearl; it should gather the picture into one complete bride.

These searches lead to 2 poems in Proverbs.
The first prices Wisdom above pearls; the second prices the bride above pearls and places the merchant and good merchandise inside her portrait.
We will read each poem whole before examining its lines.
Bold type marks the words under examination.
Where a line uses a less familiar rendering, its note preserves the familiar wording and the reason for the change without interrupting the picture.
Then Scripture can answer whether the woman they describe is the *one* pearl in the heavens.

[discrete]
=== Proverbs 3: Wisdom's Poem

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 3:13-20 — MEAT rendering]
____
Blessed is the man that findeth sym:sym-wisdom[wisdom], and the man that *draweth out* sym:sym-understanding[understanding].
For the gain of her *going-round* is better than the *going-round* of silver, and her *yield* than *fine gold*.
She is *more bright than* sym:sym-pearl[pearls]: and all thy delights are not to be compared unto her.
*Length and appropriateness of days* is in her *right hand*; and in her left hand riches and *shining*.
Her ways are ways of *splendour*, and all her paths are *wholeness*.
She is a sym:sym-tree[tree] of life to them that lay hold upon her: and blessed is every one that *holdeth her fast*.
The LORD by wisdom hath founded the earth; by understanding hath he *established* the sym:sym-heaven[heavens].
By his knowledge the depths were broken open, and the *skies* drop down the sym:sym-dew[dew].
____

[discrete]
=== Proverbs 3, Line by Line

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 3:13 — MEAT rendering]
____
Blessed is the man that findeth wisdom, and the man that *draweth out understanding*.footnote:fn31draweth[The KJV reads __“the man that getteth understanding.”__ The Hebrew verb _puq_ (H6329) can mean to issue, bring forth, or draw out; __draweth out__ keeps that attested sense.]
____

The poem begins with the merchant's action: he *finds*.
Understanding is not purchased from outside; it is drawn from the Word like treasure brought out of a field.
The same search will end with the wife: __“whoso findeth a wife findeth a good thing”__ (Proverbs 18:22).

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 3:14 — MEAT rendering]
____
For the gain of her *going-round* is better than the going-round of silver, and her *yield* than *fine gold*.footnote:fn31goinground[The KJV reads __“the merchandise of it”__ and __“the gain thereof.”__ Strong's gives H5503, the root beneath both forms of _sachar_, as __“to travel round (specifically as a pedlar).”__ BDB lists _tevuah_ as __“product, yield”__ and treats its use here as Wisdom's figurative gain.]
____

Merchandise is what that traveling trader gains; the MEAT rendering keeps the root's motion audible.
*Yield* is what a field, a tree, or a life produces.
The line joins the merchant's circuit to Wisdom's yield.
Its opening phrase, __“her merchandise is good,”__ returns in the bride's portrait, where she tastes that her merchandise is good (Proverbs 31:18).
The pearl parable has entered Solomon's vocabulary before a pearl is named.

The verse prices Wisdom against a second treasure: her yield is better than *fine gold* — _charuts_, gold as mined.
What gold contributes to the poem is not its price but its property, and Scripture develops that property from text to text.
Job moves from __“bright light”__ in a cleansed sky to _zahav_, the ordinary gold-word (Job 37:21-22).footnote:fn31fairweather[The KJV renders _zahav_ here as __“fair weather.”__]
The Song portrays the Bridegroom's head as fine gold and His hands as gold rings, then sets bright ivory beside sapphire (Song of Solomon 5:11, 14).
Solomon covered the sanctuary in gold and set ten golden lamps before the most holy place (1 Kings 6:20-22; 7:49), and the holy city John saw is __“pure gold, like unto clear glass”__ under the light of God's glory (Revelation 21:18, 23).
Gold does not yet define Wisdom's yield; it gives the poem a visible property to carry forward: luster — received light made visible.
The next line calls Wisdom bright; the line after it gives her shining.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 3:15 — MEAT rendering]
____
She is more *bright than pearls*: and all thy delights are not to be compared unto her.footnote:fn31bright[The KJV reads __“more precious than rubies.”__ The pearl reading is documented in the note to Proverbs 3:15 above. The word rendered __precious__ can also describe brightness; the KJV itself uses it for __“the moon walking in brightness”__ (Job 31:26).]
____

The poem therefore prices Wisdom above pearls in the moon's own vocabulary: precious, and heard again, bright.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 3:16 — MEAT rendering]
____
*Length and appropriateness of days* is in her right hand; and in her left hand riches and *shining*.footnote:fn31daysshining[The KJV reads __“length of days”__ and __“riches and honour.”__ The word translated __length__, _orek_, can also describe what reaches or fits its appointed point. The word behind __shining__, _kavod_, is glory or honour, displayed as radiance when the LORD's glory rises and His people shine (Isaiah 60:1).]
____

The line therefore holds both the count of days and their fitness — time measured and time appointed.
Glory or honour is displayed here as radiance.

The hands also carry direction.
Strong's gives the right hand as the south and the left as the dark or northern side.
The complete witness holds the days in her bright hand and their shining even in her dark one.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 3:17 — MEAT rendering]
____
Her ways are ways of *splendour*, and all her paths are *wholeness*.footnote:fn31splendour[The KJV reads __“ways of pleasantness”__ and __“paths are peace.”__ _Noam_ includes beauty, delight, suitability, and splendour; _shalom_ includes completeness, welfare, and wholeness as well as peace.]
____

A full witness walks a complete path.
The poem is beginning to describe not merely a jewel but a light completing its appointed course.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 3:18 — MEAT rendering]
____
She is a tree of life to them that lay hold upon her: and blessed is every one that *holdeth her fast*.footnote:fn31holdfast[The KJV reads __“happy is every one that retaineth her.”__ The Hebrew verb _tamak_ can mean to retain, grasp, sustain, or hold fast.]
____

It is the action the bride's palms will perform when they hold the circuit.
It is also the verb of Moses' hands held steady — _emunah_, faithfulness — until the going down of the sun (Exodus 17:12).
The Tree of Life also keeps the moon's measure: it bears 12 fruits and yields its fruit __“every month”__ (Revelation 22:2).
Wisdom is held as the faithful witness holds its course.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 3:19, KJV]
____
The LORD by wisdom hath founded the earth; by understanding hath he *established* the sym:sym-heaven[heavens].
____

The poem now tells us where its picture belongs.
The Hebrew verb translated *established*, _konen_ (H3559), is echoed when David looks upon __“the moon and the stars, which thou hast *ordained*”__ (Psalm 8:3).
The Wisdom priced above pearls is the Wisdom that built the sky: __“when he prepared the heavens, I was there”__ (Proverbs 8:27).

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 3:20 — MEAT rendering]
____
By his knowledge the depths were broken open, and the *skies* drop down the sym:sym-dew[dew].footnote:fn31skies[The KJV reads __“the clouds drop down the dew.”__ The word translated __clouds__, _shachaqim_, can also name the fine skies.]
____

The depths recall the fountains of the flood (Genesis 7:11), while the fine sky is where the faithful witness is established (Psalm 89:37).
The poem ends with the heavens opened above and the measured waters below.
Moses joins the same deep and dew to __“the precious fruits brought forth by the sun”__ and __“the precious things put forth by the moon”__ (Deuteronomy 33:13-14).
Its Wisdom belongs to the ordered creation whose lights govern days, months, and appointed times.

[discrete]
=== Eight Verses, One Complete Picture

The count is striking: 8 verses, with the lunar thread unbroken in every one.
Verse 13 gives the merchant's *finding* of the heavenly pearl; verse 14, the *going-round* and gold's luster; verse 15, the *bright pearl*; verse 16, measured days, appointed time, direction, and shining; verse 17, the complete path; verse 18, the Tree of Life yielding every month and held fast; verse 19, the moon established in the heavens; and verse 20, the deep and dew joined to what the moon puts forth.
No verse drops the thread.
The poem has not merely compared Wisdom with a pearl; it has drawn one complete pearl across the whole sky.

__But wait, there's more.__

[discrete]
=== Proverbs 31: The Bride's Portrait

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:10-31 — MEAT rendering]
____
A woman of valour who can find? for her *price is far above* sym:sym-pearl[pearls].
The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, and gain shall *never diminish*.
She doeth him good and not evil all the days of her life.
She seeketh wool, and flax, and worketh willingly with her *palms*.
She is like the ships of *the one who travels round*; she bringeth her sym:sym-bread[bread] *from afar*.
She riseth also while it is yet sym:sym-night[night], and giveth sym:sym-meat[meat] to her household, and *the appointed portion* to her maidens.
She considereth a sym:sym-field[field], and *buyeth* it: with the sym:sym-fruit[fruit] of her *palms* she planteth a vineyard.
She girdeth her loins with *strength*, and strengtheneth her arms.
She *tasteth that it is good*, her merchandise: her sym:sym-lamp[lamp] goeth not out *in the night*.
She layeth her hands to the spindle, and her *palms hold fast the circuit*.
She spreadeth out her *palm* to the sym:sym-poor[poor]; yea, she reacheth forth her hands to the needy.
She is not *afraid of the whiteness* for her household: for all her *lineage wraps in years*.
She maketh herself coverings; her clothing is *white linen* and *royal maroon*.
Her husband is known in the sym:sym-door[gates], when he sitteth among the sym:sym-elders[*elders*] of the land.
She maketh *fine linen*, and selleth it; and delivereth girdles unto the *merchant*.
Strength and *splendour* are her clothing; and she *laugheth at the last day*.
She openeth her mouth with sym:sym-wisdom[wisdom]; and in her tongue is the law of kindness.
She *keepeth the watch* over the *walkings* of her household, and eateth not the sym:sym-bread[bread] of *idleness*.
Her sons arise, and call her blessed; her husband also, and he *maketh her shine*.
Many daughters have done valiantly, but thou hast *gone up above them all*.
Charm is a lie, and beauty a *vapour*: a woman that feareth the LORD, *she it is that shall shine*.
Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her own works *make her shine in the* sym:sym-door[gates].
____

[discrete]
=== Proverbs 31, Line by Line

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:10 — MEAT rendering]
____
A woman of valour who can find? for her *price is far above pearls*.
____

The first poem opened with a man who finds Wisdom; this one opens by asking who can find the woman.
The Hebrew noun _chayil_ names strength or valour.
The same pearls that priced Wisdom now price the woman.
The thing the Merchant seeks has now been given a woman's form.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:11 — MEAT rendering]
____
The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, and gain shall *never diminish*.footnote:fn31diminish[The KJV reads __“he shall have no need of spoil.”__ The noun _shalal_ can mean spoil or gain, while _chaser_ can mean to lack, decrease, or fail; the rendering keeps both alternate senses together.]
____

The faithful wife does not diminish her husband's gain; she sustains and reflects it.
In the heavenly portrait, her husband is the sun, and his gain is the light seen upon her.
Her whole visible face receives and faithfully returns his light.
The line points specifically to the full moon, not a waxing or waning one.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:12, KJV]
____
She doeth him good and not evil all the days of her life.
____

This is submission expressed as covenant faithfulness, not passivity.
Her life is ordered toward the good of her husband.
The moon likewise serves the office appointed by its head through every one of its days.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:13 — MEAT rendering]
____
She seeketh wool, and flax, and worketh willingly with her *palms*.footnote:fn31palms[The KJV renders _kaph_ simply as __“hands.”__ The more specific noun names the palm, the hollow of a hand, or the bowl of a dish.]
____

The Hebrew noun is _kaph_, the palm, rather than the more general word for hand; Strong's traces it to _kaphaph_, __“to curve,”__ and uses the same noun for the hollow of a hand and the bowl of a dish.
The palm is the open, curved face of the hand — a vessel made to receive, hold, and cover.
Job places light in that same vessel: __“By two palms He hath covered the light”__ (Job 36:32, YLT).
Flax is the stalk-fiber that is spun and woven into linen.
The poem begins with wool and flax as raw material; by verse 22 she is clothed in white linen, and by verse 24 she makes fine linen.
The bride is already preparing the garments by which her deeds will be made visible.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:14 — MEAT rendering]
____
She is like the ships of *the one who travels round*; she bringeth her sym:sym-bread[bread] from afar.footnote:fn31travelsround[The KJV reads __“the merchant's ships.”__ _Socher_ can name a trader and belongs to the same travel-and-trade family as _sachar_ in Proverbs 3:14.]
____

The merchant-word returns.
Her sym:sym-bread[bread] is the Word: __“man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD”__ (Deuteronomy 8:3).
That Word is __“a lamp unto my feet, and a sym:sym-light[light] unto my path”__ (Psalm 119:105).
Psalm 19 gives speech to the heavens, sends their words to the end of the world, and then shows the sun running his circuit (Psalm 19:1-6).
The earthly woman brings bread home by merchant ship; in the heavenly hearing, the bride brings her Husband's Word from above and bears it through the night as light while she travels her appointed course.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:15 — MEAT rendering]
____
She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her household, and *the appointed portion* to her maidens.footnote:fn31portion[The KJV reads __“a portion to her maidens.”__ _Choq_ can name a portion, appointment, statute, or fixed time—the word-family used for the ordinances of the moon and stars in Jeremiah 31:35. Only __appointed__ is an alternate lexical sense here; the covenant connection comes from the scriptural cross-reference.]
____

The light has now entered the night.
Of all the lights, the full moon rises as darkness falls and remains through the night.

The meat-word itself, _teref_, is unchanged; Psalm 111:5 joins that same meat to remembrance of the covenant.
The bride distributes the calendar's own food at the appointed time.

Jesus names that exact office:

[quote.scripture, Matthew 24:45, KJV]
____
Who then is a *faithful and* sym:sym-wise[wise] *servant*, whom his lord hath made ruler over his *household*, to give them sym:sym-meat[meat] *in due season*?
____

Jesus calls the servant both *faithful* and sym:sym-wise[wise].
Proverbs has attached sym:sym-wisdom[Wisdom] to the woman, while Psalm 89 attaches the title sym:sym-faithful-witness[Faithful Witness] to the sym:sym-moon[moon].
The woman performs the deed of that faithful and wise servant: under her lord, she gives the household meat at the appointed time.
Her food and her light are both received; she gives neither her own word nor her own calendar, but faithfully delivers what her head appointed.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:16, KJV — “palms” restored]
____
She considereth a sym:sym-field[field], and *buyeth* it: with the fruit of her *palms* she planteth a vineyard.
____

The sym:sym-field[field] is the world, and the vineyard is the house of Israel (Matthew 13:38; Isaiah 5:7).
The sym:sym-moon[moon's] meaning follows the covenant relationship: bride → Messiah → Father.
Under Messiah, the moon represents the sym:sym-marriage[bride] receiving her Bridegroom's light; under the Father, it represents Messiah receiving and bearing His Father's light.
The woman remains the bride in Proverbs' plain portrait, but the lunar figure can carry both relationships.
As the bride, she is the sym:sym-pearl[pearl] Messiah purchased; in the moon's other relational role, the field-buyer is Messiah, purchasing the field for the treasure hidden within it (Matthew 13:44).
The parable of the gold hidden in the field has returned through the moon's other office, and the vineyard planted within that field identifies the treasure as Israel.
Proverbs 31 now holds both adjacent parables: verse 10 supplies the sym:sym-pearl[pearl] and its price; verses 14 and 18 supply the merchant and good merchandise; verse 16 supplies the sym:sym-field[field] and its purchase.
Solomon has bound the pearl and the field into one portrait.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:17, KJV]
____
She girdeth her loins with strength, and strengtheneth her arms.
____

Daniel sees the same pattern in a body filled with light:

[quote.scripture, Daniel 10:5-6, KJV]
____
Then I lifted up mine eyes, and looked, and behold a certain man clothed in *linen*, whose *loins were girded with fine gold* of Uphaz:
His body also was like the beryl, and his *face as the appearance of lightning*, and his *eyes as lamps of fire*, and his *arms* and his feet like in colour to *polished brass*, and the voice of his words like the voice of a multitude.
____

The portraits align line by line.
Her flax becomes white linen; Daniel's man is clothed in linen.
She girds her loins with strength; his loins are girded with fine gold.
She strengthens her arms; his arms shine like polished brass.
In the next line her sym:sym-lamp[lamp] does not go out in the night; his face flashes like lightning and his eyes are lamps of fire.
Later she opens her mouth with sym:sym-wisdom[wisdom]; the voice of his words sounds like a multitude.

The figure then touches Daniel and strengthens him: __“Be strong, yea, be strong … thou hast strengthened me”__ (Daniel 10:18-19).
He does not merely display strength; he gives it.
The woman likewise strengthens what she plants, and her lamp bears light into the night.
The sequence reveals the moon's Messiah-role in the woman's portrait: what comes from the Head is faithfully carried and given onward.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:18 — MEAT rendering]
____
She *tasteth that her merchandise is good*.footnote:fn31tasteth[The KJV reads __“she perceiveth that her merchandise is good.”__ The verb can also mean __tasteth__.] Her sym:sym-lamp[lamp] goeth not out *in the night*.
____

The same __“it is good”__ was spoken over the light (Genesis 1:4), and the same merchandise was introduced in Proverbs 3:14.
Now its lamp burns in the night.
Wisdom, bride, merchant, good, and light have arrived in one sentence.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:19 — MEAT rendering]
____
She layeth her hands to the spindle, and her *palms hold fast the circuit*.footnote:fn31circuit[The KJV reads __“her hands hold the distaff.”__ The plain housewife reading is valid: _pelekh_ names a spindle or whorl. A spindle whorl is a small weighted disk fitted around a spindle to keep it turning evenly while fiber is twisted into thread.]
____

The word also comes from roundness and can carry the sense of a circuit; the MEAT line gives that second hearing while preserving the spinning image.
The housewife holds the spinning tool; the heavenly bride holds the round.
The palm supplies the open, curved face; the circuit supplies the circle.
Together they form the full moon's open face, receiving light and holding its appointed course.
The verb *hold fast*, _tamak_, is the one Wisdom used in Proverbs 3:18.
The two poems touch palm to circuit and hold it in place.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:20 — MEAT rendering]
____
She spreadeth out her sym:sym-palm[palm] to the sym:sym-poor[poor]; yea, she reacheth forth her hands to the sym:sym-poor[needy].
____

The open face now turns outward and gives what it received.
The same curved palm introduced in verse 13 now opens toward the poor — in Scripture's sense of the word: the bowed and empty-handed before God, not merely those short of money.
That is the King's signature: __“He shall deliver the needy when he crieth; the poor also”__ (Psalm 72:12).
The same psalm sets this mercy __“with the sun and *before the face of the moon*”__ through all generations (Psalm 72:5).

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:21 — MEAT rendering]
____
She is not *afraid of the whiteness* for her household: for all her *lineage wraps in years*.
____

The familiar pointed reading — __“not afraid of the *snow*… clothed with *scarlet*”__ — already contributes to the lunar portrait: snow is white and scarlet is red, the 2 colors of the ordinary full moon and the blood moon.
It also prepares the white linen and royal maroon of the next verse.
But that is one reading; the unpointed letters carry additional hearings.
The word for *house*, _bayit_, can also name a lineage, and the verb rendered *wraps*, _labash_, properly means to wrap around and, by implication, to clothe.
The consonants under __“scarlet”__ can be heard as _shanim_, years, or _shnayim_, double.footnote:fn31clothing[The Septuagint, Vulgate, and Smith's Literal Translation support doubled garments; the Masoretic pointing reads scarlet. The same consonants permit _shanim_, years. The several readings are kept visible rather than collapsed.]
The years wrap around her household: successive months circle through generations, gathering them into the completed count the lights were made to measure.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:22 — MEAT rendering]
____
She maketh herself coverings; her clothing is *white linen* and *royal maroon*.footnote:fn31linenmaroon[The KJV reads __“silk and purple.”__ _Shesh_ names bleached linen rather than silk. _Argaman_ names the costly murex-dyed cloth of royalty and the sanctuary; its historical color range includes wine, burgundy, and dark maroon rather than only modern violet.]
____

The first term names bleached linen; the second, the costly murex-dyed cloth of royalty and the sanctuary.
This is semantic drift hiding a meaning that the symbolic language recovers.
Read alone, *purple* suggests the modern violet or lilac range; read beside the preceding snow and scarlet, the surrounding witnesses confirm the white-and-red pair.
White linen and royal maroon preserve that same pair in the bride's clothing.
The full moon's ordinary face is white; under eclipse the same complete face becomes blood-dark and royal maroon.
The 2 colors belong to one garment and one witness.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:23, KJV]
____
Her husband is known in the gates, when he sitteth among the elders of the land.
____

The husband is the sun of this portrait, and Psalm 19 gives the sun the form of a bridegroom running his appointed course:

[quote.scripture, Psalm 19:5-6, KJV]
____
Which is as a *bridegroom* coming out of his chamber, and rejoiceth as a strong man to *run a race*. His going forth is from the end of the heaven, and his *circuit* unto the ends of it.
____

He is known in the gates of that circuit and seated among the sym:sym-elders[elders] of the heavenly host.
The wife is not an independent light; her position and glory identify the head whose light she bears.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:24, KJV]
____
She maketh fine linen, and selleth it; and delivereth girdles unto the merchant.
____

The Merchant who sought the pearl now appears inside her portrait and receives the work of her hands.
Her 2 wares — fine linen and girdles — match the clothing of the luminous man already seen in Daniel: he is __“clothed in linen”__ and his loins are __“girded with fine gold”__ (Daniel 10:5).
The Son of man likewise appears __“girt about the paps with a golden girdle”__ (Revelation 1:13), while Revelation calls the bride's fine linen __“the righteous acts of the saints”__ (Revelation 19:8, NKJV).
The bride does not purchase the Merchant; her faithful deeds bear His likeness and return to the One who purchased her.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:25 — MEAT rendering]
____
Strength and splendour are her clothing; and she *laugheth at the last day*.footnote:fn31lastday[The KJV reads __“she shall rejoice in time to come.”__ The verb _sachaq_ means “laugh,” and _le-yom acharon_ means “at the last or latter day.” Young's, Douay-Rheims, and Smith's preserve this reading.]
____

The word behind *splendour*, _kavod_, can display honour as radiance.
Scripture defines the last day as the day of resurrection: __“I will raise him up at the last day”__ (John 6:39-40, 44, 54), and Martha confesses that her brother __“shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day”__ (John 11:24).
It is also the day of judgment, when the Word judges the one who rejected it (John 12:48).
Beneath the laugh-verb, the same consonants can be heard as _shachaq_, the sky where the moon is established as a faithful witness (Psalm 89:37).
The rest of the portrait now follows in order: her sons *arise*, her Husband *makes her shine*, and she has *gone up above* all the daughters (Proverbs 31:28-29).
The full-moon bride does not merely rejoice at an indefinite future; she laughs at the day of resurrection.
The link:/books/symbolic-language/return-on-the-full-moon/[Return on the Full Moon] chapter follows that day through the Prophets and Revelation — and shows why it is her phase.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:26, KJV]
____
She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue is the law of kindness.
____

The bride speaks with the Wisdom of the first poem.
Her nightly testimony is the speech of Psalm 19: the heavens declare, and their line goes through all the earth.
What she declares is law, delivered kindly by a faithful witness rather than imposed by an independent ruler.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:27 — MEAT rendering]
____
She *keepeth the watch* over the *walkings* of her household, and eateth not the bread of idleness.footnote:fn31watch[The KJV reads __“she looketh well to the ways of her household.”__ _Tsaphah_ is the watchman's word; _halikhah_ can mean a procession, course, or walking.]
____

She watches the ordered walkings of her house, as Job sees __“the moon walking in brightness”__ (Job 31:26).
The witness keeps watch because the household's course marks time.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:28 — MEAT rendering]
____
Her sons arise, and call her blessed; her husband also, and he *maketh her shine*.footnote:fn31makethshine[The KJV reads __“her husband also, and he praiseth her.”__ The verb _halal_ can mean both to praise and to shine.]
____

The senses meet here: the husband praises her by making her shine.
This is the sun-moon relationship stated without naming either light — her brightness comes from her husband, and the household sees it.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:29 — MEAT rendering]
____
Many daughters have done valiantly, but thou hast *gone up above them all*.footnote:fn31goneup[The KJV reads __“thou excellest them all.”__ _Alah_ can mean to go up, ascend, or surpass; the rendering preserves the upward motion.]
____

She rises above the daughters as the full witness rises above the lesser lights.
The next biblical portrait will call her the one woman above the daughters and identify her openly with the moon.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:30 — MEAT rendering]
____
Charm is a lie, and beauty a vapour: a woman that feareth the LORD, *she it is that shall shine*.footnote:fn31shallshine[The KJV reads __“favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain… she shall be praised.”__ _Hevel_ is breath or vapour, while _halal_ again carries both praise and shining.]
____

Surface beauty passes.
The light that remains is the sym:sym-fear[fear of the LORD] worked into faithful obedience.
Again _halal_ joins praise and shining.
The bride shines because she reflects the judgment and character of her Head.

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:31 — MEAT rendering]
____
Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her own works *make her shine in the gates*.footnote:fn31worksshine[The KJV reads __“let her own works praise her in the gates.”__ The verb is again _halal_; __make her shine__ keeps the same alternate sense used in verses 28 and 30.]
____

The portrait ends with sym:sym-fruit[fruit], sym:sym-works[deeds], sym:sym-light[light], and sym:sym-door[gates].
Revelation clothes the bride in the righteous deeds of the saints and makes each gate of her city one pearl (Revelation 19:8; 21:21).
Her works do not buy her husband; they make visible the light of the Husband who bought her.

Through all 22 lines the poem never uses the word *moon*.
It paints a woman who rises in the dark, shines through the night with light her husband gives her, distributes appointed portions, holds the circuit, walks in brightness, and shines in the gates.
Then the Song of Songs supplies the withheld name:

[quote.scripture, Song of Solomon 6:9-10]
____
My dove, my undefiled is but *one*; she is the *only one* of her mother, she is the choice one of her that bare her.
The daughters saw her, and *blessed* her; yea, the queens and the concubines, and they *praised* her.
Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, *fair as the* sym:sym-moon[moon], clear as the sym:sym-sun[sun], and terrible as an army with banners?
____

The poem paints the portrait; the Song signs it.
The one woman above the daughters is the moon toward the sun — the bride under her husband, bearing his light.

[discrete]
=== The Sapphire Form

Scripture places sym:sym-sapphire[sapphire] inside the same wisdom-and-pearl chain.
Job names __“the precious onyx, or the sapphire”__; two verses later, the same price-list declares, __“the price of wisdom is above *pearls*”__ (Job 28:16, 18).
Lamentations returns to the pearl and adds its colors:

[quote.scripture, Lamentations 4:7-8, KJV — “pearls” restored]
____
Her *Nazarites* were purer than *snow*, they were *whiter* than *milk*, they were more *ruddy*footnote:fn31ruddy[“Ruddy” means red or reddish in color.] in body than sym:sym-pearl[pearls]footnote:fn31peninim[], their polishing was of sym:sym-sapphire[sapphire]:
Their visage is *blacker* than a *coal*; they are not known in the streets: their skin cleaveth to their bones; it is withered, it is become like a stick.
____

The passage follows the same Nazarites through a terrible reversal.
They had been pure as snow, white as milk, ruddy beside pearls, and polished like sapphire.
Under the famine their appearance became black, their skin withered against their bones, and the people who once knew them no longer recognized them in the streets.
The white, ruddy, pearl, and sapphire comparison describes their former splendour; the blackness measures how completely that splendour was lost under judgment.
The reversal also gives the preceding chapter's counterfeit a human face: __“darkness for light, and light for darkness”__ (Isaiah 5:20).
The people once distinguished by purity and brightness are made to wear the opposite.

Scripture defines sapphire's office elsewhere.
Moses first places it beneath God's feet:

[quote.scripture, Exodus 24:10 — “clearness” clarified]
____
And they saw the God of Israel: and there was under his feet as it were a paved work of a sym:sym-sapphire[sapphire] stone, and as it were the body of sym:sym-heaven[heaven] in its *brightness*.footnote:fn31clearness[The KJV reads __“in his clearness.”__ Here __clearness__ means visible brightness or luster, not ease of understanding. The Hebrew _tohar_ (H2892) ranges from purity to brightness; Psalm 89:44 renders it __“glory,”__ while the Septuagint renders this phrase __“in its purity.”__ The surrounding sapphire, sky, and glass imagery supplies the reflective surface.]
____

Ezekiel then sees the same stone above the firmament:

[quote.scripture, Ezekiel 1:26, KJV]
____
And above the firmament that was over their heads was the *likeness of a throne*, as the appearance of a sym:sym-sapphire[sapphire] stone: and upon the likeness of the throne was the likeness as the appearance of a man above upon it.
____

Ezekiel 10:1 repeats the same sapphire likeness above the cherubim.
The unpointed word is כסא.
Point it as _kisse_ and the sapphire has the likeness of a *throne*; hear the same consonants as _keseh_, the word Proverbs 7:20 uses for the *full moon*, and the sapphire in the firmament has the likeness of the full moon.
Both hearings stand in the letters, and Psalm 89 makes the pairing explicit by setting the throne as the sun and establishing it as the moon.
Scripture has given the lunar throne a mineral likeness: sapphire is the full moon in its enthroned form.

Scripture itself unfolds this *brightness*.
The Hebrew word behind it grows from *clean* and appears only 4 times: twice for the days of __“purifying”__ (Leviticus 12:4, 6), once for this bright sapphire pavement — and once more as *glory* in the psalm of the throne:

[quote.scripture, Psalm 89:44, KJV]
____
Thou hast made his *glory* to cease, and cast his throne down to the ground.
____

Purifying, brightness, glory — one word spans them all, and it names a shining that is *worn*.
The king's glory can be made to *cease* because a reflector's light was never its own.

Job hangs the mirror in the same sky.

[quote.scripture, Job 37:18 and 21, KJV]
____
Hast thou with him spread out the sky, which is strong, and as a *molten looking glass*?

And now men see not the *bright light* which is in the clouds: but the wind passeth, and *cleanseth* them.
____

The mirror is the very heaven where the psalm's faithful witness stands (Psalm 89:37).
Three verses after naming it, Job shows what happens when the wind passes over it.
The sky is a cast mirror; to cleanse it is to clear it until the light comes through; and the pavement under the God of Israel is __“the body of heaven”__ in exactly that brightness — a pure surface returning light.
John keeps the geometry in the throne room: __“before the throne”__ stands __“a sea of glass”__ — *before* in the sense of *in the face of* (Revelation 4:6).
What faces a light returns it, and the sym:sym-sea[Sea & Waters] study in Part Six will meet that mirror-sea and the temple's copy of it.

The law's mirror and the sky's mirror are one surface.
James sets the hearer before __“a mirror”__ that shows a man __“his natural face,”__ and names the glass: __“the perfect law of sym:sym-liberty[liberty]”__ (James 1:23-25) — the Word shows a man himself.
Paul turns the same glass toward its Owner: __“we all, with open face *beholding as in a glass* the glory of the Lord, are *changed into the same image* from glory to glory”__ (2 Corinthians 3:18).
One mirror — the Word — gives back both faces, and the looking transforms the one into the other.
The moon is that mirror hung in the sky: the faithful witness bearing light not his own, as __“the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, and we beheld his *glory*”__ (John 1:14).

Marriage completes the portrait.
The Song places sapphire within the husband-and-wife figure: the Beloved is white and ruddy, bright ivory overlaid with sapphires; the one woman is __“fair as the moon, clear as the sun”__ (Song of Solomon 5:10, 14; 6:9-10).
Isaiah calls the woman's Maker her Husband, then promises, __“I will lay thy foundations with sapphires”__ (Isaiah 54:5, 11).
Revelation calls the holy city __“the bride, the Lamb's wife,”__ sets sapphire as its second foundation, and makes every gate one pearl (Revelation 21:9, 19, 21).

The pearl names the full moon by visible form — one, white, round, complete.
Sapphire names the same witness by throne and marriage office.
Revelation seals the union in one Bride-city: sapphire in the foundations, one pearl at every gate.

[discrete]
=== The One Pearl of the Night Sky
Notice the pearl's properties as Scripture handles the figure.
It is *one*: the merchant found __“one pearl of great price”__ and stopped collecting, for the kingdom is not a collection but one bride, bought whole.
It is *round and complete*: the roundness sits inside Strong's definition itself.
It is *white* — a bearer of soft, borrowed light out of darkness — and it is born of the *waters*.
Then Revelation prices the city's entrances in it:

[quote.scripture, Revelation 21:21]
____
And the twelve sym:sym-door[gates] were twelve *pearls*; *every several gate was of one pearl*…
____

The Greek doubles the point — _each one_ of the gates, _of one_ pearl — and the Hebrew Revelation doubles it the same way: every *single* gate, of *one* pearl.
Not gates studded with pearls: each gate *is* one pearl — one, complete, whole.
So the pearl, wherever Scripture uses it, is the one complete thing of great price — and it is a *gate*.
Now ask the merchant's question: has the King hung such a thing anywhere in plain sight — one, round, white, complete, and standing at a door?

Look up.
Of all the moon's phases and all the lights of heaven, exactly one is white, round, and complete: the night sky owns precisely one pearl.
And Scripture had already assigned that light its office: the moon appointed for the _moedim_, the appointed times, from the fourth day (Psalm 104:19; Genesis 1:14).

The pairing was set at the pattern's founding: Joseph's dream read the moon as the *mother* (Genesis 37:9-10), and the sun comes out of his chamber __“as a *bridegroom*”__ (Psalm 19:5) — a bridegroom's answering light is his bride, the counterpart that the link:/books/symbolic-language/sun-moon-and-stars/[Sun, Moon, and Stars] chapter already seated facing him, moon toward her Bridegroom as the Son is moon toward His Father.

[discrete]
=== The Letters Confirm It

If the pearl has led truly, the letters should be waiting at the same spot — and they are.
Scripture keeps a __“fulness”__ overhead.
The Hebrew is _keseh_ — Strong's: __“*fulness* or the *full moon*”__ — and Psalm 81 places it on the feast day:footnote:fn31keseh[The King James prints __“in the time appointed.”__ The NKJV, ESV, NASB, JPS, and Smith's Literal Translation read *full moon*. The Septuagint calls it the conspicuous or well-marked day of the feast. The Hebrew contains no __“and”__ separating new moon from full moon; translations that insert one divide what the sentence presents together.]

[quote.scripture, Psalm 81:3, NKJV]
____
Blow the trumpet at the time of the New Moon, at the *full* sym:sym-moon[moon], on our solemn feast day.
____

Of the moon's phases exactly one is full and conspicuous, while the dark conjunction is the one day the sky shows no sign at all.
The Hebrew places the new-moon trumpet, the full moon, and the festival sacrifice on one day: the full moon is the head of the month and feast-day of Numbers 10:10 and 28:11.

Solomon uses the same word for the day the traveling husband returns: __“he will come home at the *full moon*”__ (Proverbs 7:20) — _keseh_ again — and there it is spelled כסא, letter for letter the spelling of _kisse’_, __“throne.”__
The last chapter stood on that identity from the enemy's side; here is the LORD's side of it. Both words grow from one root, _kasah_, to cover, to fill — the throne is the covered seat, the full moon the filled light — and Job holds the two senses up in a single verse: __“He holdeth back the face of *his throne*, and spreadeth *his cloud* upon it”__ (Job 26:9), the veiled face of His full sym:sym-moon[moon].

If it is asked which way the covering runs — whether the throne-word is covered in darkness or covered in light — Scripture describes the throne itself.
Daniel saw the throne-room itself, and every detail belongs to this chapter:

[quote.scripture, Daniel 7:9, NKJV]
____
I watched till *thrones* were *put in place*, and the *Ancient of Days* was seated; His garment was *white as snow*, and the hair of His head like *pure wool*. His throne was a *fiery flame*, its wheels a burning fire.
____

The thrones are *put in place* like lights in their stations.
And the title under __“Ancient of days”__ is built on a root of moving onward, going before — read once, He is the Ancient of Days; read again, He is the *Foremost of Days*: the One at the head of the days, seated where the days begin.
His garment white as snow, His hair like the pure wool, His throne flame, His wheels burning fire — and the plural on __“wheels”__ is the ending this book met on Daniel's sevens: an intensive, not a count — *the wheel complete*, the perfect circle of fire.

Whiteness enthroned on light; brightness round about it, __“as the appearance of the sym:sym-bow[bow] that is in the cloud in the day of rain”__ (Ezekiel 1:26-28); and its Occupant __“coverest thyself with *light* as with a garment”__ (Psalm 104:2).
If the throne is the _keseh_, Daniel's vision draws what the letters spell: the full moons set in their stations, and the Head of Days taking His seat — white, complete, covered in light — where the month begins.

The psalm that gave this book the sym:sym-faithful-witness[faithful witness] link:/books/symbolic-language/sun-moon-and-stars/[already sets the throne] as the sym:sym-sun[sun] and as the sym:sym-moon[moon] — Psalm 89:36-37 — plain simile, not wordplay, and the throne is a throne of light.footnote:fn26thronepsalm[Derived in the link:/books/symbolic-language/sun-moon-and-stars/[Sun, Moon, and Stars] chapter.]
Where darkness stands near it, it stands *outside*, as a veil: __“clouds and darkness are *round about* him”__ (Psalm 97:2) — round about, not within — the cloud of Job 26:9 spread *upon* the face, holding the light back.
The _keseh_ is covered in light; only the counterfeit is covered in dark.

[discrete]
=== The Gate That Opens

The sky is built like a sanctuary — the tabernacle Psalm 19 pitched for the sun — and its front, like the tabernacle's, faces the sunrise, the sym:sym-east[east].
Now hear Ezekiel on the gates of the house:

[quote.scripture, Ezekiel 46:1]
____
Thus saith the Lord GOD; The sym:sym-door[gate] of the inner court that looketh toward the sym:sym-east[east] shall be *shut the six working days*; but on the *sabbath* it shall be opened, and in the day of the *new* sym:sym-moon[moon] it shall be opened.
____

Three kinds of days — working days, sabbaths, new-moon days (Amos knew the third kind too: __“When will the *new moon* be gone, that we may sell corn?”__ Amos 8:5) — and on the day that begins the month, the east gate stands open.
A gate is opened because something is meant to come through it.
Exactly one phase enters by the east gate at the fall of night: the *full* moon enters in the east at the hour already fixed by the portrait — through the front door of the sky's tabernacle, the faithful witness at maximum.

The sliver, by contrast, is hunted low in the *west*, at sunset, beside the sun — and the sheepfold has a rule about entrances:

[quote.scripture, John 10:1-2]
____
Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that entereth not by the sym:sym-door[door] into the sheepfold, but *climbeth up some other way*, the same is a *thief* and a robber.
But he that entereth in by the sym:sym-door[door] is the *shepherd* of the sheep.
____

The prince of Ezekiel's house comes and goes __“by the way of the gate that looketh toward the *east*”__ (Ezekiel 46:12).
The true light enters at the front sym:sym-door[gate]; the counterfeit climbs in from the dark side — which is precisely the address his heart chose in the last chapter.

[discrete]
=== One Pearl, One Gate

Now set the pieces together.
The pearl is the full moon; the city's pearl-gates are His appointed times — for the _moedim_ are, as the last chapter read the word, *meetings*: the fixed days on which the King receives.
Twelve gates; twelve months of full moons; the sym:sym-stars[stars] of God gathered into the twelve constellations, the __“Mazzaroth”__ brought forth __“in his season”__ (Job 38:32), through which the full moon makes its yearly round.
And there Solomon's woman collects what her portrait promised — praised in the gates her fulness passes through, her husband at home among the elders.

The Merchant who sold all He had was not buying His own entrance into the kingdom.
He was purchasing the Bride-city whose people are His treasure and whose gates are pearls — the bride gathered to meet her King at His appointed times.
Isaiah had already welded the paired parables into one sentence: __“sym:sym-wisdom[wisdom] and knowledge shall be the stability of thy *times*… the sym:sym-fear[fear] of the LORD is his *treasure*”__ (Isaiah 33:6).
The treasure and the bride; the pearl and the gate; the King and the appointed meeting.

__“It is the glory of God to *conceal* a thing: but the honour of kings is to *search out* a matter”__ (Proverbs 25:2) — He hid the bride's portrait where the Merchant who would give everything for her was already looking.

[discrete]
=== Pearls Before Swine

Jesus uses the word *pearl* only once more, and there it carries a warning:

[quote.scripture, Matthew 7:6]
____
Give not that which is *holy* unto the sym:sym-dog[dogs], neither cast ye your *pearls* before *swine*, lest they *trample them under their feet*, and turn again and rend you.
____

The dogs and the swine are one family — unclean sym:sym-beast[beasts], the nations outside the covenant table.
And what swine do to pearls is exactly what Scripture says the nations do to holy things: they tread them underfoot — __“it is given unto the *Gentiles*: and the holy city shall they *tread under foot*”__ (Revelation 11:2); the sanctuary and the host __“*trodden under foot*”__ (Daniel 8:13); __“Jerusalem shall be *trodden down* of the Gentiles, until the *times* of the Gentiles be fulfilled”__ (Luke 21:24).

The sentence ends on *times*: even the trampling has an appointed limit.
If the pearl is the appointed time of meeting, the warning reads whole: hand the holy times to the nations, and they will not keep them — they will trample them, and turn and rend the hand that gave them.
Daniel named the plan — to change the times and the laws; this verse is the Lord's advance notice of how the theft would look on the ground — the pearl underfoot.

[discrete]
=== The Two Moons

Read this chapter and the last as the pair they are.
The enemy raises the moon covered in *darkness*; the LORD's sign is the same seat covered in *light* — the Father's whole face borne through the dark.
One moon reflects everything; the other reflects nothing, for its source produces only dark.
One enters by the door; the other climbs up some other way.

The sky itself stages the ambition, for the two moons stand in two different places: the full moon, standing always opposite, can never come between; only the moon covered in darkness can stand *over* the sun — slide before his face and put out the day at noon — and blot the sym:sym-stars[stars] from the same sky.
That is the plan of the last chapter drawn in one picture — __“Woe unto them… that put *darkness for light*, and *light for darkness*”__ (Isaiah 5:20).

The sym:sym-stars[stars] — the righteous, who keep time — follow one moon or the other.
That is why the parable's Merchant sells *all*: the pearl is not an ornament a sinner purchases from the kingdom; it is the bride the Son redeems, pictured at the gate where she meets her King.
Only the Son could pay that price, and Scripture says He paid it gladly.

Grade this chapter the way the Parables of the Kingdom chapter graded everything, for the method matters more than any single finding.
Every link stands in the text: wisdom and the bride priced above _peninim_; the city's gates each of *one pearl*; the moon set over the _moedim_ from the fourth day; _keseh_, the full moon, sharing the letters of __“throne”__; the east gate opened on the new-moon day; and the two poems painting the same light from beginning to end.
The chain that joins the links is a reading — this book's reading, offered to be tested, not swallowed.

The reckoning that follows from it — where the month truly begins, how the sabbaths fall, what history did to the calendar and what the sky and the records of the nations still testify — is a book of its own.footnote:fn26ttt[The complete case is made in _Time Tested Tradition: The Renewed Biblical Calendar_.]
This chapter needs only the symbol.
The kingdom has a gate; the gate is one complete pearl; and the Bridegroom gave all to purchase the bride who meets Him there.

The appointed times the pearl governs are counted in sevens — and the word Scripture counts them with is the next chapter.

sources.name: 31x-return-on-the-full-moon.adoc
sources.content:
---
title: "Return on the Full Moon"
slug: return-on-the-full-moon
order: 31.5
permalink: /books/meat-bibles-symbolic-language/return-on-the-full-moon/
description: "The prophets give the Day of the LORD a shape before anyone asks for its date: the Husband comes home at the full moon and the shofar sounds at that phase; the coming shines from east to west while evening remains light; the moon shines as the sun; sun and moon face one another, silenced, in Joshua's rehearsal of the Day; and the whole moon becomes blood. Read with Scripture's own definitions, the witnesses agree on the configuration — the full moon — while refusing the year and the day. Then the full-moon bride's laughter at the last day needs no explaining."
og_title: "Return on the Full Moon — MEAT The Bible's Symbolic Language"
epigraphs:
  - quote: "He hath taken a bag of money with him; he will come home at the full moon."
    ref: "Proverbs 7:20, ASV"
---
The prophecies of the Day of the LORD are written in words this book has already defined: sym:sym-sun[sun], sym:sym-moon[moon], sym:sym-day[day], sym:sym-night[night], sym:sym-east[east] and west, trumpet, silence.
Read them the way every symbol in this book has been read — each word taken to where Scripture uses it — and the prophets sketch not the date of that Day but its *configuration*: how the sky is arranged when it arrives.
Here is the claim to be tested: every physical mark the prophets give the Day of the LORD is a mark of the *full moon*, and no mark requires any other phase.
The witnesses come from the Writings, the Law's own history, the Prophets, the Gospels, and Revelation — and they agree on the phase while still concealing the date.
Yet the phase alone eliminates 97% of the possible days: one day in a month of 29 or 30 keeps the appointment hidden and still narrows the search to the night the moon is full.

[discrete]
=== The Appointment: Husband, Trumpet, Resurrection

Scripture names the phase in its portrait of an absent husband:

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 7:19-20, ASV]
____
For the man is not at home; he is gone a long journey:
He hath taken a bag of money with him; he will come home at the *full moon*.
____

The pointed text reads that phase-word, _keseh_, in exactly one other place — and there it carries the trumpet:

[quote.scripture, Psalm 81:3, NKJV]
____
Blow the *trumpet* at the time of the New Moon, at the *full moon*, on our solemn feast day.
____

Paul places the resurrection at a trumpet: __“the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised”__ (1 Corinthians 15:52), and __“the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise”__ (1 Thessalonians 4:16).
Set the three side by side and they are one scene.
Proverbs gives the returning Husband; the psalm gives the shofar; Paul gives the shout, the coming Lord, and the dead arising — and both texts the pointing reads as _keseh_ put the homecoming and the trumpet at the full moon.
That count — two — is the Masoretes' count, not the letters'.
Unpointed, _keseh_ and _kisse'_, the *throne*, are the same consonants in the same two spellings; the phase-word the points confine to two verses shares its letters with the seat of every king in Scripture.
The full moon and the throne were never two words — a second witness that the Husband who comes home at the full moon comes home to *reign*.

[discrete]
=== The Geometry of the Day

A full moon is not merely a brighter moon.
It is the one phase in which sym:sym-sun[sun] and sym:sym-moon[moon] face one another from opposite sides of the earth.
As the sun sets in the west, the full moon rises in the sym:sym-east[east].
It crosses the night and remains visible in the sym:sym-west[west] when the sun returns in the east.
The whole night is held between 2 facing lights.

.The geometry of fulness — opposition above, the observer's night below
image::geometry-of-the-day.svg["Top: the full moon stands opposite the sun with the earth between, while the new moon sits dark beside the sun and the quarter at right angles. Bottom: at evening the full moon rises in the east as the sun sets in the west; at dawn the sun's light out of the east finds the moon setting in the west",pdfwidth=86%,align=center]

Isaiah states the condition plainly, and names the day it belongs to:

[quote.scripture, Isaiah 30:26, KJV]
____
Moreover the light of the *moon shall be as the light of the sun*, and the light of the *sun shall be sevenfold*, as the light of seven days, in the day that the LORD bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.
____

The moon in this verse is _levanah_, the white or bright moon — the same word used when the bride is __“fair as the moon”__ (Song of Solomon 6:10).
Isaiah does not leave a crescent partly dark; the moon receives the glory of the sun while the sun bears seven days of light.
Whatever power produces that promised brightness, the portrait requires the moon's complete face — and the verse pins it to the day the LORD binds up the breach of His people.

Two more witnesses hint at the same arrangement.
Zechariah circles that day and leaves a strange mark on its evening:

[quote.scripture, Zechariah 14:6-7, NKJV]
____
It shall come to pass in that day that there will be no light; the lights will diminish.
It shall be one day which is known to the LORD — neither day nor night. But at evening time it shall happen that it will be *light*.
____

The day's own name seals it: __“one day”__ is _yom echad_, and _echad_ is the whole — __“the *whole* congregation *together*”__ (Ezra 2:64) — not one long day of unbroken light, but the *Whole-day*: the day of the whole sym:sym-moon[moon], whose evening is light.
At every other phase the moon rises either before or after sunset.
At fulness it rises opposite the setting sun.
Evening arrives, yet light rises from the other horizon.

Jesus draws His coming with the same span of sky:

[quote.scripture, Matthew 24:27, KJV]
____
For as the *lightning cometh out of the east*, and *shineth even unto the west*; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.
____

_Astrapē_ can name lightning or a bright shining; Luke uses it for the bright shining of a lamp (Luke 11:36).
A flash of lightning owns no compass; light that comes *out of the east* and shines *even unto the west* is the sun's.
At fulness that shining crosses the whole sky and lands on a second light: the sun comes up in the east while the whole face of the moon, setting in the west, burns with its reflected fire.
No other phase places a light in the west to answer the light out of the east.
Zechariah's evening light agrees with Matthew's east-to-west shining.
Together they form the sky Isaiah demanded — the whole face answering the sun.

[discrete]
=== When Heaven Becomes Silent

Joshua's long day gives the geometry a place in history.
From the ascent of Beth-horon, Gibeon lay toward the east and the valley of Aijalon toward the west.
Joshua addressed the sym:sym-sun[sun] over one and the sym:sym-moon[moon] over the other:

[quote.scripture, Joshua 10:12-13, KJV]
____
*Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon*; and thou, *Moon, in the valley of Ajalon*.
