And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the people had avenged themselves upon their enemies.
____

The 2 lights face one another across the sky.
That opposition is the geometry of a full moon.

The word translated __“stand still”__ is _damam_: to be still, to become silent.
Joshua's command can therefore be heard as __“Sun, be silent over Gibeon; and moon, over the valley of Aijalon.”__
The heavens become silent while the 2 great lights face one another.

Habakkuk preserves both halves of that scene.
First comes the command:

[quote.scripture, Habakkuk 2:20, KJV]
____
But the LORD is in his holy temple: let all the earth *keep silence before him*.
____

The next chapter sees the battle:

[quote.scripture, Habakkuk 3:11, KJV]
____
The *sun and moon stood still* in their habitation: at the light of thine arrows they went, and at the shining of thy glittering spear.
____

Revelation places the same silence immediately before the trumpets:

[quote.scripture, Revelation 8:1-2, KJV]
____
And when he had opened the seventh seal, there was *silence in heaven about the space of half an hour*.
And I saw the seven angels which stood before God; and to them were given seven trumpets.
____

The later Book of Jasher is not Scripture, but it preserves an interesting historical expansion of the event Scripture itself says was recorded in Jasher (Joshua 10:13).
Its account says the sun stood still __“six and thirty moments”__ while the moon also stood still (Jasher 88:63-64).footnote:fnlastdayjasher[The later Book of Jasher is cited here only as an outside witness to a remembered duration, not as authority for doctrine. Its __“36 moments”__ cannot be converted into modern minutes with certainty, but it is notably close to Revelation's __“about the space of half an hour.”__]
Revelation says about half an hour; Jasher preserves 36 moments.
Neither supplies the other, but both remember a measured silence in heaven.

Joshua's battle also tells us why this event belongs to the Day of the Lord.
God casts great hailstones from heaven, killing more than Israel's sword; Revelation ends the plagues with hailstones weighing about a talent (Joshua 10:11; Revelation 16:21).
Five kings flee into a cave and great stones close its mouth; at the sixth seal the kings of the earth hide in dens and among the rocks, begging the rocks to hide them from the face of the enthroned King (Joshua 10:16-18; Revelation 6:15-17).
The facing lights are not an isolated wonder.
They stand inside a small-scale rehearsal of the final judgment.

Joshua's earlier conquest of Jericho carries the same order.
Jericho's name belongs to the Hebrew moon-family; Israel keeps silent before the shout, the trumpets sound, the wall falls, the harlot's household is brought out, and then the city burns (Joshua 6:10, 20-24).
Silence, trumpet, deliverance, fall, and fire appear at the moon city before Revelation repeats them across the world.

[discrete]
=== The Whole Moon Becomes Blood

The prophets do not merely place a moon near the Day of the Lord.
They describe its face:

[quote.scripture, Joel 2:30-31, KJV]
____
And I will shew wonders in the heavens and in the earth, blood, and fire, and pillars of smoke.
The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the *moon into blood*, before the great and the terrible day of the LORD come.
____

John sees the same pair when the sixth seal opens:

[quote.scripture, Revelation 6:12 — literal Greek]
____
The sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the *whole moon became as blood*.
____

The word _holē_, omitted from many English renderings, means whole or entire.
John sees not a thin red edge but the moon's complete face.
The full phase is the phase that presents the whole illuminated face to the earth.

Joel places blood, fire, and pillars of smoke beside the darkened sun and blood-red moon.
Revelation likewise darkens the sun and air with smoke (Revelation 9:2), while Babylon's burning sends up smoke visible from afar (Revelation 18:9, 18).
Whether the blood color comes through eclipse, smoke, or the direct act of God, the sign requires an illuminated moon capable of displaying a complete blood-red face.

This is why the prophets' repeated darkness matters.
Amos calls the Day of the Lord __“darkness, and not light”__; Joel calls it __“a day of darkness and of gloominess”__; Zephaniah calls it __“a day of clouds and thick darkness”__ (Amos 5:18-20; Joel 2:2; Zephaniah 1:15).
Darkness falling on the brightest night of the month is itself a sign.
The faithful witness that should be white becomes blood; the sun that should illuminate it becomes black.

[discrete]
=== One Phase, Many Witnesses

No single comparison carries the conclusion alone.
The force is in their convergence:

* the Husband returns home at the full moon;
* the shofar sounds at the full moon, and the Lord descends with the trumpet as the dead arise;
* the coming shines from east to west, while at evening there is light;
* the moon shines as the sun while the sun carries seven days of light;
* sun and moon face one another in Joshua's Day-of-the-Lord rehearsal and become silent;
* heaven keeps a measured silence before the trumpets; and
* the sun turns black while the whole moon becomes blood.

These witnesses do not name a modern date, a particular year, or even which full moon of the year.
They establish the structure before anyone attempts the calendar arithmetic.
The last day is repeatedly drawn with the physical marks of the full moon.
What the reader carries away is a decoded expectation: when the trumpet sounds, the sky is at fulness.

[discrete]
=== Why She Laughs

Now the full-moon bride's strangest line needs no explaining:

[quote.scripture, Proverbs 31:25 — MEAT rendering]
____
Strength and splendour are her clothing; and she *laugheth at the last day*.footnote:fn-last-day-laugh[The King James renders the ending “she shall rejoice in time to come.” The verb _sachaq_ means “to laugh,” and _le-yom acharon_ means “at the last or latter day.”]
____

Scripture defines the last day as the day of resurrection and judgment: __“I will raise him up at the *last day*”__ (John 6:39-40, 44, 54); __“I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the *last day*”__ (John 11:24); the Word judges at the last day (John 12:48).
Laughter joined to that approaching sym:sym-day[Day] is Scripture's picture of confidence in how it will unfold: the LORD laughs at the kings gathered against His Anointed (Psalm 2:4); He laughs at the wicked man because __“he seeth that his day is coming”__ (Psalm 37:13); and those who weep now __“shall laugh”__ in __“that day”__ (Luke 6:21-23).
He laughs because rebellion's appointed Day is coming; she reflects His laughter because that same Day is her deliverance.

The last day is her phase.
Her Husband comes home at the full moon.
The trumpet sounds.
Her children *arise*, her Husband *makes her shine*, and she has *gone up above* all the daughters (Proverbs 31:28-29).
The night's weeping becomes joy in the morning (Psalm 30:5); the dead arise and the living are __“caught up together with them… to meet the Lord”__ (1 Thessalonians 4:16-17).
The lunar portrait ends at the resurrection, laughing.

The four spirits sent to carry that Day across the whole earth wait in link:/books/symbolic-language/the-four-winds/[The Four Winds].

sources.name: 31y-clouds-of-heaven.adoc
sources.content:
---
title: "Clouds of Heaven"
slug: clouds-of-heaven
order: 31.75
permalink: /books/meat-bibles-symbolic-language/clouds-of-heaven/
description: "Genesis puts the covenant bow in the cloud. Psalms calls the clouds God's chariot; Isaiah says He rides one; Ezekiel opens the cloud and reveals cherubim, wheels, a throne, its Rider, and the bow; Psalm 89 directly compares that throne to the moon, and its Hebrew consonants identify the full-moon phase; Revelation repeats the enthroned figure upon a white cloud and a white horse."
og_title: "Clouds of Heaven — MEAT The Bible's Symbolic Language"
epigraphs:
  - quote: "Who maketh the clouds his chariot: who walketh upon the wings of the wind."
    ref: "Psalm 104:3"
---
Genesis places the covenant bow in the cloud, and it is almost universally understood as a rainbow.
Yet the Bible's symbolic language reveals a much deeper meaning that yields profound insight throughout Scripture.
This chapter lets Scripture interpret Scripture, showing that the clouds of heaven are God's chariot and are associated with the full moon, which serves as His throne and guides the steps of His people.

Noah states the connection directly:

[quote.scripture, Genesis 9:13, 16]
____
I do set my *bow in the cloud*… And the bow shall be *in the cloud*; and I will look upon it, that I may remember the everlasting covenant.
____

The covenant bow is assigned a location.

[.scripture-pair%unbreakable]
--
Scripture then names what the cloud is:

[quote.scripture, Psalm 104:3]
____
Who layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters: who maketh the *clouds his chariot*: who walketh upon the sym:sym-wings[*wings*] of the sym:sym-wind[*wind*].
____
--

Isaiah supplies the corresponding action:

[quote.scripture, Isaiah 19:1]
____
Behold, the LORD *rideth upon a swift cloud*.
____

Israel's cloud-pillar likewise governed the timing of the nation's walk through the wilderness: when the cloud lifted they journeyed, and while it remained they camped (Exodus 40:36-37; Numbers 9:17-23).

Ezekiel then opens the chariot-cloud:

[quote.scripture, Ezekiel 1:4-5]
____
Behold, a whirlwind came out of the north, a *great cloud*, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it…
Also out of the midst thereof came the likeness of four living creatures… and they had the likeness of a man.
____

The things moving within the cloud appear as fire and light:

[quote.scripture, Ezekiel 1:13-14]
____
As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of fire, and like the appearance of *lamps*… and the fire was bright, and out of the fire went forth lightning.
And the living creatures ran and returned as the appearance of a *flash of lightning*.
____

Ezekiel later says, __“I knew that they were the *cherubims*”__ (Ezekiel 10:20).
Chronicles names their office:

[quote.scripture, 1 Chronicles 28:18]
____
The *chariot of the cherubims*, that spread out their wings, and covered the ark of the covenant of the LORD.
____

[.scripture-pair%unbreakable]
--
The vision now rises above the cherubic chariot:

[quote.scripture, Ezekiel 10:1]
____
Then I looked, and, behold, in the firmament that was above the head of the *cherubims* there appeared over them as it were a sym:sym-sapphire[*sapphire*] stone, as the appearance of the likeness of a *throne*.
____
--

The linked symbol supplies the identification: sym:sym-sapphire[Sapphire] is the full moon in its enthroned form.
Without the points beneath the throne-word, the final phrase may also be heard, __“as the appearance of the likeness of a full moon.”__
Ezekiel then reveals the One seated there:

[quote.scripture, Ezekiel 1:26]
____
And above the firmament that was over their heads was the likeness of a *throne*, as the appearance of a sym:sym-sapphire[sapphire] stone: and upon the likeness of the throne was the likeness as the appearance of *a man above upon it*.
____

The vision closes by returning to Noah's bow:

[quote.scripture, Ezekiel 1:27-28]
____
I saw as the colour of amber, as the appearance of fire round about within it… and it had brightness round about.
As the appearance of the *bow that is in the cloud* in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness round about.
This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD.
____

[discrete]
=== The Throne as the Moon

Scripture makes the throne–moon comparison directly:

[quote.scripture, Psalm 89:36-37]
____
His seed shall endure for ever, and his *throne as the* sym:sym-sun[sun] before me.
It shall be established for ever *as the* sym:sym-moon[moon], and as a sym:sym-faithful-witness[faithful witness] in heaven.
____

The word rendered __“before me”__ is _neged_ — before, in front of, facing, opposite.
The full moon alone occupies that relation to the sun: the two lights face one another from opposite sides of the earth.

.The throne before the sun — in front, facing, opposite
image::geometry-of-the-day.svg["Top: the full moon stands opposite the sun with the earth between, while the new moon sits dark beside the sun and the quarter at right angles. Bottom: at evening the full moon rises in the east as the sun sets in the west; at dawn the sun's light out of the east finds the moon setting in the west",pdfwidth=86%,align=center]

At the dark phase, the illuminated hemisphere faces away from the earth; at the full phase, the moon stands opposite the sun and the face visible from earth is covered with the sun's light.
The chariot psalm gives the same covering:

[quote.scripture, Psalm 104:2-3]
____
Who *coverest thyself with light* as with a garment… who maketh the *clouds his chariot*.
____

Daniel's throne is fire, and Ezekiel's cloud-borne throne shines with fire, brightness, and the bow round about it (Daniel 7:9; Ezekiel 1:26-28).
The full moon is the sym:sym-faithful-witness[faithful witness] covered with the greater light and bearing it toward the earth.

Job then lays the cloud directly over the face of the *throne (full moon)*:

[quote.scripture, Job 26:9, ASV]
____
He incloseth the face of his *throne*, and spreadeth his *cloud* upon it.
____

Above the cloud-borne chariot is the throne with its Rider: the full-moon seat with its Rider enthroned.

[discrete]
=== The Bow Around the Throne

John now sees the bow around the throne itself:

[quote.scripture, Revelation 4:2-3]
____
Behold, a *throne* was set in heaven, and *one sat on the throne*… and there was a *rainbow round about the throne*, in sight like unto an emerald.
____

Genesis places the bow in the cloud; Ezekiel reveals its brightness around the glory above the cloud-borne throne; Revelation places it around the throne itself.
Ezekiel's stated likeness is the bow __“in the day of rain,”__ and within that same vision it surrounds the throne Scripture compares to the moon.
Through most of its visible changing, the moon itself appears as a bow carried toward and away from fulness.
The covenant reminder is thereby rehearsed across most of the month.

[discrete]
=== The Rider of the Clouds

Daniel gives the cloud its royal passenger:

[quote.scripture, Daniel 7:13-14]
____
One like the *Son of man came with the clouds of heaven*, and came to the sym:sym-ancient-of-days[Ancient of days]… And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom.
____

Read as a title, He is the Venerable One whose throne is established of old. Read as calendar language, He is seated at the advancement of days—the beginning from which the month, year, and age proceed.

Jesus claims Daniel's scene before the high priest:

[quote.scripture, Matthew 26:64]
____
Hereafter shall ye see the *Son of man* sitting on the right hand of power, and *coming in the clouds of heaven*.
____

At His ascension the cloud receives Him:

[quote.scripture, Acts 1:9, 11]
____
While they beheld, he was taken up; and a *cloud received him* out of their sight… this same Jesus… shall so *come in like manner* as ye have seen him go into heaven.
____

The cloud receives the Rider and carries Him from sight; the angels make that manner of departure the manner of return.

[discrete]
=== White Cloud, White Horse

John next sees the Rider upon a white cloud:

[quote.scripture, Revelation 14:14]
____
And I looked, and behold a *white cloud*, and *upon the cloud one sat* like unto the Son of man, *having* on his head a golden *crown*, and in his hand a sharp sickle.
____

The same rider-formula returns upon a white horse:

[quote.scripture, Revelation 6:2]
____
And I saw, and behold a *white horse*: and *he that sat on him had a bow*; and a *crown* was given unto him: and he went forth conquering, and to conquer.
____

Both visions place a seated, crowned figure upon something white; one is a cloud, the other a horse, and the horse-rider carries the bow Genesis placed in the cloud.
John elsewhere sees Faithful and True seated upon a white horse when heaven opens (Revelation 19:11).

Zechariah completes the bridge:

[quote.scripture, Zechariah 6:3, 5]
____
In the *third chariot white horses*… These are the four *spirits of the heavens*, which go forth from standing before the Lord of all the earth.
____

In Revelation, the white cloud and white horse occupy the place beneath the seated figure; Psalms calls the cloud a chariot, and Zechariah joins white horses to a chariot.

[discrete]
=== The Definition

*Cloud* — the visible covering and mobile throne-chariot of heaven: it manifests and veils its Rider's presence, bears the throne, and carries those received into it.
In prophetic rider scenes, the white cloud occupies the same conveyance-position as the white horse.

sources.name: 32-the-sabbath.adoc
sources.content:
---
title: "The Sabbath"
slug: the-sabbath
order: 32
permalink: /books/meat-bibles-symbolic-language/the-sabbath/
description: "A sabbath can be complete (Leviticus 23:15) — and only a span can be complete or broken. The law states the equation itself: Leviticus counts 'seven sabbaths' where Deuteronomy counts 'seven weeks' — and Hebrew owns a bare week-word, so the choice teaches. The word names the whole seven — six days of labor and one of rest as a single unit — a unit the temple hymnal divides into numbered days, the law separates from its own seventh day by grammar (the day OF the sabbath), and Scripture scales to years, to jubilees, and to the great week whose seventh millennium is the rest that remains. The seventh day itself is the day of the LORD's work: the rest is from your own works, while the offering doubles and mercy stays lawful."
og_title: "The Sabbath — MEAT The Bible's Symbolic Language"
epigraphs:
  - quote: "…from the morrow after the sabbath, from the day that ye brought the sheaf of the wave offering; seven sabbaths shall be complete."
    ref: "Leviticus 23:15"
---
Ask what the word _sabbath_ names and every answer points at one day in seven.
But the law counts sabbaths — and watch what it says about them:

[quote.scripture, Leviticus 23:15]
____
And ye shall *count* unto you from the morrow after the sabbath, from the day that ye brought the sheaf of the wave offering; *seven sabbaths shall be complete*.
____

A sabbath can be *complete* — the word is _temimot_, whole, unblemished, the word the law uses for a sacrifice without defect — and whatever can be complete can be incomplete.
A day cannot be partially itself; it is or it is not.
Only a *span* can be whole or broken.
The thing Israel counts toward Pentecost is not seven rest-days; it is seven unbroken *sevens* — and the word for that unit is _sabbath_.

[discrete]
=== The Law States the Equation

This is not an inference; the law says it twice, once in each vocabulary.
The same omer count that Leviticus gives as __“seven *sabbaths*”__ stands in Deuteronomy as:

[quote.scripture, Deuteronomy 16:9]
____
*Seven weeks* shalt thou number unto thee: begin to number the seven weeks from such time as thou beginnest to put the sickle to the corn.
____

One command, one festival, one count — _sabbath_ in Leviticus, _week_ in Deuteronomy.
The equation is stated by parallel statute: **a sabbath is a week** — the complete seven, of which the day of rest is the seventh part.

Hebrew is not short of week-words.
When Laban says __“fulfil her *week*”__ (Genesis 29:27), the word is _shavua_ — a bare seven of days — and it is Deuteronomy's word for the omer count itself.
Leviticus had that word available and wrote _shabbatot_ instead.
The choice is part of the statute: a _shavua_ is any seven; a _sabbath_ is the seven structured by rest — six days of labor closed by a holy seventh — and only a structured seven can be _temimot_, whole or broken.

[discrete]
=== A Day's Name Over Its Block

The objection is natural: perhaps _sabbath_ is simply the rest-day's name, borrowed loosely for the span it closes.
Scripture answers with the calendar's own grammar, because naming a block of days by its marked day is exactly how the feasts talk:

[quote.scripture, Ezekiel 45:21]
____
In the first month, in the fourteenth day of the month, ye shall have the *passover, a feast of seven days*; unleavened bread shall be eaten.
____

The passover is one day's sacrifice, slain on the fourteenth — yet Ezekiel names the whole seven by it, and the letters under __“seven days”__ are _shavuot yamim_: a *week* of days.
Luke records the same usage in Greek: __“the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, *which is called the Passover*”__ (Luke 22:1).
One marked day lends its name to its seven.
The passover names the week it opens; the sabbath names the week it crowns.

[discrete]
=== The Unit Scales

If _sabbath_ named only a day, it could not stretch; a unit stretches.
The law runs the same word at year-scale without changing gear: the seventh year is __“a *sabbath* of rest unto the land”__ (Leviticus 25:4), and the jubilee is reached by counting the unit squared:

[quote.scripture, Leviticus 25:8]
____
And thou shalt number *seven sabbaths of years* unto thee, seven times seven years; and the space of the seven sabbaths of years shall be unto thee forty and nine years.
____

Sabbaths *of years* — the word takes whatever tick the count assigns it: a seven of days, a seven of years, a seven of sevens.

[discrete]
=== Divided Into Days

The days of Scripture have no names.
Creation numbers them — first, second, third — and the numbering never stops: in the whole Bible no day of the week bears a name except the seventh.
The numbers live inside the sabbath, and the temple's own hymnal shows it.
The Septuagint carries the psalms Israel sang through the week, and the titles count every day as a position in the sabbath-unit: Psalm 24 is sung __“on the first day of the week”__ — _tēs mias sabbatōn_, day one *of the sabbaths* — Psalm 48 __“on the second”__ (_deutera sabbatou_), Psalm 94 __“for the fourth”__ (_tetradi sabbatōn_), and Psalm 93 __“for the day before the sabbath”__ — the _prosabbaton_, the fore-sabbath.
Mark dates the crucifixion evening by that same liturgical word: __“it was the preparation, *that is, the day before the sabbath*”__ (Mark 15:42).
Centuries before the Gospels were written, Israel was numbering its days as members of the sabbath.

The Gospels inherit the idiom whole, and translation has hidden it.
The Pharisee in the parable boasts, __“I fast twice in the week”__ (Luke 18:12) — but what he says is _dis tou sabbatou_: twice *in the sabbath*.
No man fasts twice in a day; he fasts twice in the seven — and he calls the seven _the sabbath_.
Every __“first day of the week”__ in the resurrection accounts is literally __“one of the *sabbaths*”__ — _mia sabbatōn_ (Matthew 28:1; Mark 16:2; Luke 24:1; John 20:1; Acts 20:7; 1 Corinthians 16:2) — the week's first day named as a day *of the sabbath-unit*.footnote:fnhebmatt[The Hebrew Matthew reads __“on the first day of the week”__ with _shavua_, the week-word — the old translator rendered the Greek's “one of the sabbaths” by its meaning: the unit of seven.]
Matthew holds both senses of the word in a single verse:

[quote.scripture, Matthew 28:1]
____
In the end of the *sabbath* [the day], as it began to dawn toward the first day of the *week* [literally, “one of the sabbaths” — the unit], came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary to see the sepulchre.
____

The language itself testifies: _sabbath_ names the seven, and the seventh day is its crown.

[discrete]
=== The Grammar That Marks the Day

If one word names both the week and its day, the text needs a way to say which — and it has one, the same one it uses for the month.
_Chodesh_ does the same double duty: the month, and the renewed-moon day that heads it.
Ezekiel disambiguates both words in one verse, with one construction:

[quote.scripture, Ezekiel 46:1]
____
The gate of the inner court that looketh toward the east shall be shut the *six working days*; but on the *sabbath* it shall be opened, and in the *day of the new moon* it shall be opened.
____

The Hebrew of the two clauses is identical: _b'yom ha-shabbat… b'yom ha-chodesh_ — on the *day of* the sabbath, on the *day of* the new moon.
Each unit owns a marked day, and the text names that day by the genitive.
This is the grammar of the fourth commandment itself: __“Remember the *sabbath day*”__ (Exodus 20:8) is _yom ha-shabbat_ — the day *of* the sabbath — a redundancy if _sabbath_ named only a day, and exact if the sabbath is the unit that has one.
Luke writes the rest day the same way in Greek — _tē hēmera tōn sabbatōn_, the *day* of the sabbaths (Luke 4:16; Acts 13:14; 16:13) — while the other days are numbered into the unit: the first of the sabbath, the second, the fourth.

When the law wants the resting member itself, it has a second marker: it doubles the word.
__“The seventh day is the *sabbath of rest*”__ — _shabbat shabbaton_ (Exodus 31:15; 35:2; Leviticus 23:3); the Day of Atonement receives the doubled name (Leviticus 16:31), and so does the land's seventh year (Leviticus 25:4) — the resting member at year-scale.
A counting context never doubles the word: the law says __“seven sabbaths,”__ never seven _shabbat shabbaton_.

The two senses sort themselves by one rule: *numbers count the unit; conduct lands on the day.*
Counts take the block — __“seven sabbaths shall be complete,”__ __“seven sabbaths of years.”__
Conduct takes the day — kindle no fire (Exodus 35:3), bake and seethe beforehand (Exodus 16:23), the offering of the day (Numbers 28:9).
No one heals on a week; no one counts seven of a single day and calls them complete.

[discrete]
=== Six and One, One Fabric

Read the commandment again with the unit in view, and notice that it legislates all seven days:

[quote.scripture, Exodus 20:9-10]
____
*Six days shalt thou labour*, and do all thy work: But the *seventh day* is the sabbath of the LORD thy God…
____

Both clauses stand inside one commandment — the six of labor are commanded in the same breath as the one of rest.
Scripture lays the six-and-one down seven times.
Creation states it first, before the name exists — six days of making, and on the seventh God _shavat_, the verb the noun is built on (Genesis 2:2-3); the Law then writes it six times over: the manna (Exodus 16:26), the commandment and its repetition (Exodus 20:9-10; Deuteronomy 5:13-14), the covenant sign (Exodus 31:15), the assembly at Sinai (Exodus 35:2), and the appointed times (Leviticus 23:3) — every one, __“six days… but the seventh day is the sabbath.”__
Seven times the composition, never once the day alone.
Such repetition is redundant if _sabbath_ names a day defined by rest — a rest-day needs stating once; it is exactly right if the word names a seven defined by the composition of its parts, for a whole is defined by giving all its parts — and Scripture never gives the sabbath any other way.
The same formula runs over the years — __“Six years thou shalt sow thy field… but in the seventh year shall be a sabbath of rest unto the land”__ (Leviticus 25:3-4) — and it outlives Sinai: the ruler of the synagogue recites it against Jesus, __“There are six days in which men ought to work… and not on the sabbath day”__ (Luke 13:14) — a hostile witness, still defining the sabbath by its six.

The sabbath is not an interruption of the week; it is the week made whole, six-and-one as one fabric.
To keep the seventh is to confess the ownership of all seven — the rest-day is one-seventh of what the word names, and the six days of labor are as much *inside the sabbath* as the rest is.

The block is given, not privately counted.
Israel's first weeks out of Egypt were marked from heaven by the bread itself:

[quote.scripture, Exodus 16:29]
____
See, for that the LORD hath *given you* the sabbath, therefore he giveth you on the sixth day the bread of two days; abide ye every man in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.
____

Double bread on the sixth day, none on the seventh — a schedule no man could move, marking the whole unit and not merely its end.
The temple ran on the same block: the courses of priests and guards __“enter in *on the sabbath*”__ and __“go forth *on the sabbath*”__ (2 Kings 11:5, 7, 9) — a week of duty bounded by the word, service reckoned sabbath to sabbath.

[discrete]
=== The Day of the LORD's Work

The commandment says __“in it thou shalt not do any work”__ — and the same law commands work in it.

[quote.scripture, Numbers 28:9-10]
____
And *on the sabbath day* two lambs of the first year without spot, and two tenth deals of flour for a meat offering, mingled with oil, and the drink offering thereof: This is *the burnt offering of every sabbath*, beside the continual burnt offering, and his drink offering.
____

The offering *doubles* on the seventh day.
The shewbread is baked and set in order __“every sabbath”__ (Leviticus 24:8; 1 Chronicles 9:32); circumcision proceeds on the sabbath __“that the law of Moses should *not* be broken”__ (John 7:23).
Jesus states it flatly: __“on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and *are blameless*”__ (Matthew 12:5).
The law that forbids work on the seventh day assigns more of its own work to that day than to any other.

The rest command carries the resolution in its own wording.

[quote.scripture, Isaiah 58:13]
____
If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing *thy pleasure* on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the LORD, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing *thine own ways*, nor finding *thine own pleasure*, nor speaking *thine own words*:
____

The prohibition is possessive — _thy_ pleasure, _thine own_ ways, _thine own_ words — and Hebrews reads the seventh day of creation with the same possessive: __“he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from *his own* works, as God did from his”__ (Hebrews 4:10).
God's own seventh day was no idle day — __“on the seventh day God *ended his work*”__ (Genesis 2:2), and the blessing and hallowing of the day are acts *of* the day; __“My Father worketh hitherto, and I work”__ (John 5:17) is his Son's answer to a sabbath accusation.
The shape of the unit is now complete: six days belong to your work, and the seventh is not empty — it is the day of *his*: the convocation, the doubled offering, and the mercy that is __“lawful to do well on the sabbath days”__ (Matthew 12:12).
Rest is not the absence of work; it is whose work fills the day.

[discrete]
=== The Great Week

Now scale the unit by the prophetic day — for __“one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day”__ (2 Peter 3:8) — and the sabbath opens into the calendar of the whole age.
Six days of labor, then the day of rest; six thousand years of toil, then __“There remaineth therefore a *rest* to the people of God”__ (Hebrews 4:9) — and the word there is _sabbatismos_, a sabbath-keeping.
The thousand-year reign is not an isolated doctrine; it is the seventh-part of a sabbath whose whole is seven thousand years — the great week, complete.
The unit that orders the week and the land and the jubilee orders the age, because it was never a day's name; it was the name of the complete seven at whatever scale the LORD counts.
The great week keeps the six-and-one shape of its smallest copy: __“Let us *labour* therefore to enter into that rest”__ (Hebrews 4:11) — the labor now, the sabbath ahead.

[discrete]
=== The Standing Triad

Scripture reckons time in a standing triad — the feast, the new moon, the sabbath: the year, the month, and the seven between them.
The gate of Ezekiel's vision opens for exactly two kinds of day: the day of the sabbath and the day of the new moon (Ezekiel 46:1-3).
The Shunammite's husband asks why she rides to the prophet when __“it is *neither new moon, nor sabbath*”__ (2 Kings 4:23); the grain merchants wait out both — __“When will the *new moon* be gone, that we may sell corn? and the *sabbath*, that we may set forth wheat?”__ (Amos 8:5); Isaiah's restoration runs __“from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another”__ (Isaiah 66:23); Paul lists __“an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days”__ as one triad (Colossians 2:16).
The month is divided into sabbaths, and the sabbath into days — and the law itself pins rest-days to the month's dates: at Tabernacles, __“on the first day shall be a sabbath, and on the eighth day shall be a sabbath”__ (Leviticus 23:39) — the *fifteenth* and the *twenty-second* of the month.

[discrete]
=== The Count That Convicts the Calendar

The count exposes a paradox — and its solution must meet the text exactly.
The omer count is specified three ways at once.
It has a *fixed start*: the sheaf is waved __“on the morrow after the sabbath”__ (Leviticus 23:11), and the witnesses of the temple age — the Septuagint's rendering, Josephus's report of the practice, Israel's first Passover in the land (Joshua 5:11) — set that sheaf on the *sixteenth day of the first month*, every year.
It has a *unit-count*: __“seven sabbaths shall be complete.”__
And it has a *landing condition*: __“unto the morrow after the seventh sabbath shall ye number fifty days”__ — the fiftieth day must itself be the morrow after a sabbath.

Try to satisfy all three on an unbroken seven-day cycle, and the system jams.
A fixed sixteenth falls on a different weekday each year; count from it, and the fiftieth day is __“the morrow after the sabbath”__ only one year in seven.
The ancient parties each sawed off one leg to level the stool: some kept the fixed sheaf and let Pentecost land mid-week, abandoning the landing condition; some kept the landing and floated the sheaf to the nearest first-day, abandoning the witnessed sixteenth; some fixed both ends by fiat and abandoned the count between them.
Every camp preserved two specifications by breaking the third — and the breaks are visible, which is the point.

Notice what the continuous week does to the law's own grammar.
On an unbroken cycle, a count of sevens that begins the morrow after a sabbath *cannot produce an incomplete seven* — the qualifier __“complete”__ would legislate nothing, a dead word in a law where every word has work to do.
_Temimot_ has force only in a reckoning where a broken seven is possible — where the count can meet days that belong to no week.

There is one reckoning in which nothing breaks.
If the month itself is built of four sevens — the sabbaths standing on its eighth, fifteenth, twenty-second, and twenty-ninth days, with the renewed-moon day standing outside the sevens as the month's head — then the fifteenth is a sabbath in *every* month, the sheaf's sixteenth is *always* the morrow after the sabbath — and the numbering begins the day *after* the sheaf.

What remains of the sheaf's own week is six days: a *broken* seven, exactly what the qualifier __“complete”__ excludes.
So the count gathers seven whole sabbaths — the twenty-third of the first month through the fifteenth of the third, forty-nine days, no broken week and no renewed-moon day among them — and their morrow is the fiftieth: Pentecost on the *sixteenth of the third month*, the morrow after a sabbath, every year, the very date the Essene witnesses preserve, with no tension left in the text.
Fixed dates and weekday-landings, irreconcilable on the continuous week, agree without effort — and the triple-specified count shows itself for what it is: a *checksum*, written into the law the way redundancy is written into all Scripture, so that the true calendar passes silently, and every altered one is convicted by its own arithmetic.footnote:fn31ttt[The full case — the month of four sevens, the renewed-moon days, the witnesses for the fixed sixteenth, and the history of who changed what — is _Time Tested Tradition: The Renewed Biblical Calendar_; this chapter shows only the lock the key must fit.]

The calendar that keeps these sevens — who kept it, whose testimony carries it, and what tradition did to it — is the next chapter.

---
title: "The Four Winds"
slug: the-four-winds
order: 34
permalink: /books/meat-bibles-symbolic-language/the-four-winds/
description: "Wind, in Hebrew, is spirit (ruach). The four winds are the four spirits of heaven (Zechariah 6:5) — God's executing agents, shown in the New Testament as the four horsemen. They stir the nations, scatter and gather peoples, raise the dead, and are held or loosed at the throne's command."
og_title: "The Four Winds — MEAT The Bible's Symbolic Language"
epigraphs:
  - quote: "Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live."
    ref: "Ezekiel 37:9"
---
Prophecy is written in wind: in Hebrew, wind, breath, and spirit are one word — _ruach_.
Here we take up that symbol and fix what the four winds _are_; the sym:sym-sea[Sea] study in Part Six will meet these same winds stirring the nations.

The plainest text is Zechariah’s.
He sees four chariots drawn by colored horses come out from between two mountains of brass, and asks what they are.
The angel answers directly:

[quote.scripture, Zechariah 6:5]
____
…These are the *four spirits of the heavens*, which *go forth from standing before the Lord* of all the earth.
____

The word for __“spirits”__ is _ruach_ — the same word rendered __“wind”__ and __“breath”__ everywhere else in the Old Testament.
So the four winds are four spirits, and they hold an office: they __“go forth from standing before the Lord.”__
They are dispatched from the throne.

[discrete]
=== Not Directions, Not Weather

The dictionary flattens __“the four winds”__ two ways: into the four points of the compass — north, south, east, west, a figure for __“everywhere”__ — or into wind itself, the weather.
Scripture allows neither.
The angel did not call them four directions; he called them four _spirits_.
The number four gives them their reach — they cover the four quarters of the whole earth — but the winds are the _agents_ sent across those quarters, not the quarters themselves.

Nor are they weather.
The same word names what stands in the divine council:

[quote.scripture, Psalm 104:4]
____
Who maketh his *angels spirits*; his ministers a flaming fire.
____

Angels are spirits; spirits are winds — one word in Hebrew.
The four winds are commissioned beings: they stand before the Lord and go forth on assignment (Zechariah 6:5), then return to report (Zechariah 1:11).
And all wind answers to its Maker — He rebukes even a literal storm, __“Peace, be still,”__ and it obeys (Mark 4:39); the more so these spirit-winds He sends and recalls.
When Scripture speaks of the four winds, it speaks of God’s executing power under His direct authority.

[discrete]
=== The Four Horsemen

The New Testament shows these same four spirits under another image.
In Zechariah, they are chariots and horses; in Revelation, they are the four horsemen, commissioned one by one as the Lamb opens the seals.
The colors mark their assignments: the white sym:sym-horse[horse] goes out conquering with a sym:sym-bow[bow] — a case study of its own in Part Six; the red takes __“sym:sym-peace[peace] from the earth”__ with __“a great sym:sym-sword[sword]”__ (Revelation 6:4); the black carries scales for famine; and the fourth is Death, who carries what all four deal:

[quote.scripture, Revelation 6:8]
____
…behold a *pale* sym:sym-horse[horse]: and his name that sat on him was *Death*… to kill with sym:sym-sword[sword], and with *hunger*, and with *death*, and with the *beasts of the earth*.
____

Those four are the judgments Ezekiel had already named:

[quote.scripture, Ezekiel 14:21]
____
…my *four sore judgments*… the sym:sym-sword[sword], and the *famine*, and the *noisome beast*, and the *pestilence*…
____

They are the covenant curses of Leviticus and Deuteronomy, executed by the four spirits.
Jesus lists the same set — __“wars… famines, and pestilences”__ (Matthew 24:6-7) — and calls them __“the beginning of sorrows.”__
One sequence, recorded three times: Ezekiel’s judgments, Zechariah’s spirits, John’s horsemen.

[discrete]
=== Scatter and Gather

The four winds are not assigned to judgment only.
The same spirits carry opposite errands, according to what the throne sends.
They _scatter_ a people in judgment:

[quote.scripture, Jeremiah 49:36]
____
…upon Elam will I bring the *four winds*… and will *scatter them* toward all those winds…
____

They _gather_ a people in restoration:

[quote.scripture, Matthew 24:31]
____
…he shall send his angels… and they shall *gather together his elect* from the *four winds*, from one end of heaven to the other.
____

They _stir_ the sea so that the beast-kingdoms rise from it — __“the four winds of the heaven strove upon the great sym:sym-sea[sea].
And four great sym:sym-beast[beasts] came up”__ (Daniel 7:2-3 — a scene the sym:sym-sea[Sea] study in Part Six takes up in full).
They carry _breath_ to the dead — __“Come from the four winds, O breath… that they may live”__ (Ezekiel 37:9).
Scatter and gather, stir and raise: the wind’s direction is set by its Sender, not by itself.

The gathering has an address: the elect are collected __“from the *four winds*, from one end of heaven to the other”__ — from the four _corners_ of the earth where the dispersed wait (Isaiah 11:12), corners that the link:/books/symbolic-language/wings/[Wings] chapter searched; the winds sweep the quarters, and the quarters give up their gleanings.

The judgment-wind even has a compass habit.
It was __“a strong sym:sym-east[east] *wind*”__ that split the sea all night (Exodus 14:21); an east wind carried in the locusts (Exodus 10:13); a __“vehement east wind”__ broke Jonah (Jonah 4:8); and Hosea names whose wind it is: __“an *east wind* shall come, *the wind of the LORD*… and his spring shall become dry”__ (Hosea 13:15).

When the promised Spirit came, it came in this symbol’s own dress:

[quote.scripture, Acts 2:2]
____
And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a *rushing mighty wind*, and it filled all the house where they were sitting.
____

Ezekiel’s breath arrived on the appointed day.
Jesus had already tied the knot for Nicodemus: __“The *wind* bloweth where it listeth… so is every one that is *born of the Spirit*”__ (John 3:8) — one word for wind and Spirit, in Hebrew and in Greek alike.
Even the wind wears the covenant edge: God __“did fly upon the *wings* of the wind”__ (Psalm 18:10) — _kanphei-ruach_, the hem-word on the wind itself — and the creation psalm sets chariot, wings, and ministers side by side: __“who maketh the clouds his chariot: who walketh upon the *wings of the wind*: who maketh his angels *spirits*”__ (Psalm 104:3-4).
A wind can carry a people in that hem; the first deliverance said so — __“I bare you on *eagles' wings*, and brought you unto *myself*”__ (Exodus 19:4).

The four-going-out from the presence is older than the chariots.
The Spirit moved on the face of the waters at creation (Genesis 1:2), and the water tells the wind's story: __“a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into *four heads*”__ (Genesis 2:10) — one source at the presence, parted four ways to reach the whole earth, as the four spirits go forth from standing before the Lord.
Wind above, water below — two carriers of one _ruach_, sent out fourfold at the beginning and gathering home from the same four corners at the end.
The ones waiting at the corners complete the pattern: on the garment, the corner is where the law hangs its reminder — __“that ye may look upon it, and *remember all the commandments* of the LORD”__ (Numbers 15:39) — and at the earth's four wings wait __“the remnant… which *keep the commandments* of God”__ (Revelation 12:17).
The winds gather from the hem those who kept the hem.

[discrete]
=== Held Until the Sealing

One more fact completes the picture: the four winds can be held.
Before they are loosed, John sees them restrained:

[quote.scripture, Revelation 7:1-3]
____
…four angels… holding the *four winds* of the earth, that the wind should not blow… *Hurt not* the earth, neither the sym:sym-sea[sea], nor the sym:sym-tree[trees], *till we have* sym:sym-seal[sealed] *the servants of our God* in their foreheads.
____

The winds are kept back until God’s servants are marked.
This occurs after the sixth seal is opened (Revelation 6:12) — the riders commissioned at the first four seals are still reined in at the four corners when the sixth is broken.
The seals commission; they do not release.
Not a wind blows until the last servant is sealed.

The four winds, then, are God’s executing spirits — four because they cover the whole earth, the four quarters of heaven.
They are dispatched from the throne and recalled to it; they stir the nations, raise and topple empires, scatter and gather peoples, deal death and breathe life, and are held or loosed at a word.
They are not blind forces of nature, and not powers in revolt.
They are the ministers of the One who __“maketh his angels spirits,”__ and they do only what He sends them to do.

sources.content:
---
title: "The Fall of Babylon"
slug: the-fall-of-babylon
order: 35
permalink: /books/meat-bibles-symbolic-language/the-fall-of-babylon/
description: "The Exodus is not only history; it is the similitude of the end. The plagues replay in the vials, the call 'Come out of her, my people' repeats 'let my people go,' the pursuer sinks like a stone in both stories, and the victors stand on a sea of glass singing the song of Moses and the Lamb. The verdict is not the going down — everyone goes into the waters — but the not rising: Babylon sinks and 'shall not rise'; Jonah, the Messiah, and the baptized come up."
og_title: "The Fall of Babylon — MEAT The Bible's Symbolic Language"
epigraphs:
  - quote: "Thus shall Babylon sink, and shall not rise from the evil that I will bring upon her."
    ref: "Jeremiah 51:64"
---
When the victors over the sym:sym-beast[beast] stand on the sea of glass at the end of the story, listen to what they sing:

[quote.scripture, Revelation 15:2-3]
____
And I saw as it were a sym:sym-sea[sea] *of glass* mingled with fire: and them that had gotten the *victory over the* sym:sym-beast[beast]… And they sing the *song of Moses* the servant of God, and the *song of the* sym:sym-lamb[Lamb]…
____

Why the song of _Moses_ — the song Israel sang on the far shore of the Red Sea (Exodus 15:1)?
Because the deliverance they have just come through is the same deliverance.
The Exodus is not only history; it is the similitude of the Fall of Babylon — scene for scene, as Jonah was scene for scene the Passion.
Lay the two side by side.

[discrete]
=== The Plagues Replayed

The first plague turned the waters of Egypt to blood; the vials turn the sym:sym-sea[sea] and rivers to blood, and this time link:/books/symbolic-language/sea-and-waters/[the interpretation is spoken aloud] (Revelation 16:6).footnote:fn28bloodtodrink[The vial verses are quoted and worked in full in the link:/books/symbolic-language/sea-and-waters/[Sea & Waters] chapter.]
The waters are __“peoples, and multitudes, and nations”__ (Revelation 17:15) — the equation the sign-of-Jonah chapter first put to work — so waters turned to blood are death upon the peoples, their own shed blood given back to them; the Sea study in Part Six works the full equation.

The hands that wield the plagues are the same office.
Look at the commission of the two witnesses:

[quote.scripture, Revelation 11:6]
____
These have power to shut heaven, that it rain not in the days of their prophecy: and have power over waters to *turn them to blood*, and to *smite the earth with all plagues*, as often as they will.
____

These are Moses and Aaron’s credentials, reissued at the end of the age.
Pharaoh had his court magicians; Babylon has her sorceries (Revelation 18:23).
The contest is the same contest, at full scale.

[discrete]
=== The Rod, the Serpent, and the Rod Again

The contest opened, both times, with one enacted sign — a similitude acted out before a word was argued.
__“What is that in thine hand? And he said, A rod. And he said, Cast it on the ground. And he cast it on the ground, and it became a *serpent*”__ (Exodus 4:2-3).
The rod is no neutral stick: the Hebrew _matteh_ means *staff* and *tribe* in one word — when the princes bring twelve rods, they are the twelve tribes by the language itself (Numbers 17:2) — and Aaron's rod is the rod __“for the house of *Levi*”__ (Numbers 17:8): the priesthood in his hand.
Cast to the earth, the priesthood-rod turns serpent — and before Pharaoh the word sharpens: there it becomes a _tannin_, a sym:sym-dragon[dragon], the devouring kingdom — and __“Aaron's rod *swallowed up* their rods”__ (Exodus 7:12).
The priesthood, gone serpentine, does not merely join the dragons of the nations; it *swallows* them and rides what remains.
John saw where that ends:

[quote.scripture, "Revelation 17:5, 9, 18"]
____
And upon her *forehead* was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE *MOTHER OF HARLOTS*… The seven heads are seven sym:sym-mountain[mountains], on which the *woman sitteth*… And the woman which thou sawest is that *great city*, which *reigneth over the kings of the earth*.
____

Only a covenant partner can wear the harlot's title.
A sym:sym-harlot[harlot] is not an outsider; she is a wife gone traitor — harlotry is covenant *defected*, and only a covenant people can commit it: __“How is the *faithful city* become an harlot!”__ (Isaiah 1:21).
And this great city is identified by its crime scene: __“the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and sym:sym-egypt[Egypt], *where also our Lord was crucified*”__ (Revelation 11:8) — Jerusalem.
The woman riding the sym:sym-beast[beast] is the covenant order gone serpent — Aaron's rod cast down, astride the seven heads it swallowed — the *mother* whose daughter-harlots learned the trade in her house.
The name on her forehead is not her own.
*Babylon the Great* names the sym:sym-beast[beast] she rides, and she wears it where the sym:sym-seal[seal] goes: the saints carry the Father's name in their foreheads (Revelation 14:1); Babylon's own carry __“the *mark* of his *name*”__ (Revelation 14:11).
The wife who left her Husband's sym:sym-name[name] is branded with her owner's — the beast's mark in the seal's place.

Jeremiah's oracle fixes the last Babylon at the end in more than one sense.
__“Your *mother* shall be sore confounded… behold, the *hindermost of the nations* shall be a wilderness”__ (Jeremiah 50:12).
The Hebrew _acharith_ is the last or end — what comes after.
In the immediate judgment, the __“glory of kingdoms”__ is brought last in rank (Isaiah 13:19).
In the prophetic succession, Nebuchadnezzar's Babylon stood at the head of gold — __“thou art this head of gold”__ — while Babylon the Great appears at the latter end, when the sym:sym-stone[stone] strikes the image's feet (Daniel 2:34-35, 38, 44-45).
Babylon frames man's image: the original kingdom at its head, the final Babylon at its feet.

The word also carries a direction.
Scripture's compass faces sym:sym-east[east] — _qedem_ is at once “east” and “front” — so sym:sym-west[west] lies behind.
The related after/back/end word-family names the western sea the __“hinder sea”__ (Deuteronomy 11:24; Zechariah 14:8).
Jeremiah need not be made to choose among the layers: Babylon is brought last in rank, appears last in the imperial succession, and sits hindermost — westernmost — among the nations.
The last Babylon sits at the far west of the nations: a bloc of seven sym:sym-mountain[mountains] that even counts itself as seven, ridden by the city that killed the prophets, its base of power the westernmost nation of them all.

The similitude has a third act, and it was in Moses' hand from the beginning.
__“Put forth thine hand, and take it by the *tail*. And he put forth his hand, and caught it, and it became a *rod* in his hand”__ (Exodus 4:4).
Every word is loaded.
The tail is decoded in-text by Isaiah: __“the prophet that teacheth lies, he is the *tail*”__ (Isaiah 9:15) — the serpent is seized at its lying-prophet end.
And watch the dragon wield that member:

[quote.scripture, Revelation 12:4]
____
And his *tail* drew the third part of the sym:sym-stars[stars] of heaven, and did cast them to the earth.
____

The stars are the saints, and Daniel shows the same fall with the trampling included: the horn __“cast down some of the host and of the *stars* to the ground, and *stamped* upon them”__ (Daniel 8:10).
The dragon fells a third of heaven's host not with claws but with its tail — by the prophet that teaches lies — for __“the leaders of this people cause them to err; and they that are led of them are *destroyed*”__ (Isaiah 9:16).
The trumpet armies carry the same reversal — __“their power is in their mouth, and in their *tails*: for their tails were like unto *serpents*, and had heads”__ (Revelation 9:19) — tails grown heads, which is the covenant curse in one clause: __“he shall be the head, and thou shalt be the *tail*”__ (Deuteronomy 28:44), the inversion of the blessing that made obedient Israel __“the head, and not the tail”__ (Deuteronomy 28:13).
So the command to seize the serpent by the tail is the countermove itself: take the liar's instrument in hand, and it is mastered.
The Hebrew for __“caught”__ is _chazaq_ — the very verb of the whole contest, for __“I will *harden* [chazaq] Pharaoh's heart”__ (Exodus 4:21): the hand that chazaq-grips the serpent turns it back into the staff of God; the heart that chazaq-hardens itself belongs to the serpent.
One verb, two grips.
Revelation keeps the scene for the end: __“he *laid hold on* the dragon, that old serpent… and bound him”__ (Revelation 20:2).

The rod that comes back is not bare wood.
Set overnight before the testimony, __“the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded *almonds*”__ (Numbers 17:8) — the dead stick alive, the priesthood proven by resurrection.
The almond is the _shaqed_, the watcher-tree, first to wake — __“I see a rod of an *almond tree*… for I will *watch over* my word to perform it”__ (Jeremiah 1:11-12) — and the lampstand of the sanctuary is carved as this very tree, its bowls __“made like unto *almonds*”__ (Exodus 25:33): the watcher-tree bears the sym:sym-lamp[lamp], and the lamp, Scripture says, is the commandment (Proverbs 6:23).

An almond is a fruit that is itself a sym:sym-seed[seed] — and __“the seed is the *word of God*”__ (Luke 8:11).
Root to crown the watcher-tree carries nothing but the word: its blossom the priesthood's proof, its fruit the seed-word, its carved form the commandment's lampstand.
Rod, serpent, rod again — and then blossom: the priesthood cast down and gone dragon is seized at the liar's tail, restored to the Owner's palm, and buds with the resurrection sign.
The similitude that opened the first exodus is the arc of the last one.

[discrete]
=== Let My People Go — Come Out of Her

The demand carried to Pharaoh — __“let my people go, that they may serve me”__ (Exodus 8:1) — returns as the last call of the book:

[quote.scripture, Revelation 18:4]
____
And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, *Come out of her, my people*, that ye be not partakers of her sym:sym-sin[sins], and that ye receive not of her plagues.
____

Jeremiah had already given Babylon the same summons:

[quote.scripture, Jeremiah 51:45]
____
*My people, go ye out of the midst of her*, and deliver ye every man his soul from the fierce anger of the LORD.
____

One voice, three ages: out of Egypt, out of Babylon, out of Babylon the great.
The people of God end every act of the story by walking out of a doomed house — and the plagues fall on those who stay.

[discrete]
=== The Spoiler from the North

The destruction enters from a specific quarter.
__“For, lo, I will raise and cause to come up against Babylon an assembly of great nations *from the* sym:sym-north[north] *country*”__ (Jeremiah 50:9); __“a people shall come *from the north*, and a great nation”__ (Jeremiah 50:41); __“the *spoilers* shall come unto her *from the north*”__ (Jeremiah 51:48).
The word itself tells you why the destroyer owns that door.
__“North”__ — _tsaphon_ — is link:/books/symbolic-language/lucifers-declared-plan/[the hidden quarter], the lurker's quarter: the dark one, the direction the ambush comes from.footnote:fn28tsaphon[The word study — _tsaphan_, to hide by covering over, to lurk — is in the link:/books/symbolic-language/lucifers-declared-plan/[Lucifer's Declared Plan] chapter.]

The sym:sym-north[north] behaves this way throughout the prophets: __“out of the north an evil shall break forth”__ (Jeremiah 1:14) — and when the evil comes, it comes like a predator from cover, __“the sym:sym-lion[lion] is come up from his *thicket*, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way”__ (Jeremiah 4:7); the *spoiler*, the robber-word, falls suddenly on the unwatchful (Jeremiah 6:22-26).
Robbers work from the dark — __“in the dark they dig through houses… they know not the light”__ (Job 24:16) — and the north is the sky's own dark, the one quarter the sun never crosses.

The word carries both of its appearances in this book at once: the *north country* is the hidden quarter where Babylon's spoilers gather, and the *sides of the north* — the uttermost recesses of that dark — are the address the enemy chose for his own seat (Lucifer’s Declared Plan).
The lurker who worked from the hidden dark is repaid out of it: the spoiler comes upon Babylon from the door she cannot watch.

[discrete]
=== The Stone That Sinks

Now the ending both stories share.
When the pursuer followed Israel into the sea, the song names his end twice: __“they *sank into the bottom as a stone*”__ (Exodus 15:5); __“they *sank as lead* in the mighty waters”__ (Exodus 15:10) — __“their persecutors thou threwest into the deeps, *as a stone* into the mighty waters”__ (Nehemiah 9:11).
Jeremiah turned that ending into a commanded sign: the scroll of Babylon’s judgment bound to a stone and thrown into the Euphrates —

[quote.scripture, Jeremiah 51:63-64]
____
…thou shalt bind a *stone* to it, and *cast it into the midst of Euphrates*: And thou shalt say, Thus shall *Babylon sink, and shall not rise* from the evil that I will bring upon her…
____

Revelation performs the sign at scale:

[quote.scripture, Revelation 18:21]
____
And a mighty angel took up a stone like a great *millstone*, and *cast it into the sea*, saying, Thus with violence shall that *great city* Babylon be thrown down, and shall be *found no more at all*.
____

This is a phrase-symbol in its own right — sym:sym-cast-into-sea[cast into the sea], a ruling power sunk into the sea of peoples, never to surface; the Sea study in Part Six gathers its every use.
The sym:sym-mountain[mountain] that destroyed all the earth is rolled down and burned (Jeremiah 51:25); the millstone goes under; the music stops (Revelation 18:22).

Jesus put this very sign into His disciples' mouths, twice.
__“Whosoever shall *say unto this mountain*, Be thou removed, and be thou *cast into the sea*; and shall not doubt in his heart… he shall have whatsoever he saith”__ (Mark 11:23) — and a parallel saying runs on the other kingdom-figure: __“ye might say unto this sycamine sym:sym-tree[tree], Be thou plucked up by the root, and be thou *planted in the sea*”__ (Luke 17:6).
A mountain is a kingdom and, at this scale, a tree is a nation; what faith commands into the sea is not landscaping — it is Babylon's sentence, spoken by the household of faith.

And Revelation shows the mechanism in order: the incense goes up __“with the *prayers of all saints*”__ (Revelation 8:3-4), the censer is cast to the earth, and at the second trumpet __“as it were a great *mountain burning with fire* was *cast into the sea*”__ (Revelation 8:8) — Jeremiah's burnt mountain, over the cliff at last.
The prayers ascend; the mountain falls.
Faith that moves mountains was never about landscaping either — it is the saints praying down the destroying mountain, and being heard.

[discrete]
=== The Verdict Is the Not-Rising

The sentence keeps the going-down separate from the verdict.
Everyone in these stories goes into the waters.
Babylon sinks __“and *shall not rise*.”__

Jonah link:/books/symbolic-language/sign-of-jonah/[went into the same sea and rose]; the Messiah went into the heart of the earth and could not be held by it (Acts 2:24); and every convert enacts the split in baptism, going under into death and coming up in newness of life (Romans 6:4), his sins staying down like Babylon (Micah 7:19).footnote:fn28notrising[The rising half of the contrast is drawn scene by scene in the link:/books/symbolic-language/sign-of-jonah/[Sign of Jonah] chapter.]
The waters take everyone; the covenant decides who comes up.

The coming up is the difference between the lawless kingdom and the righteous man in the same flood — and it is why the millstone is also a personal warning: better one __“hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea”__ (Matthew 18:6) than to make the little ones stumble.
A man can be Babylon in miniature.

[discrete]
=== That Great City

Who is she?
Revelation defines both coordinates in one chapter: the sym:sym-sea[waters] where the sym:sym-harlot[whore] sitteth are the waters already identified — peoples, multitudes, and nations (Revelation 17:15) — and __“the woman which thou sawest is *that great city*, which reigneth over the kings of the earth”__ (Revelation 17:18).
The title has a history — Nineveh wore it three times (Jonah 1:2; 3:2; 4:11), and the sign-of-Jonah chapter traced where it points.
Babylon swallowed God’s people __“like a sym:sym-dragon[dragon]”__ (Jeremiah 51:34) — and the dragon, we saw with Jonah, is made to give back what it swallowed.

Revelation does more than describe the great city; it gives her street address, and gives it in the book's own symbolic grammar:

[quote.scripture, Revelation 11:8]
____
And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the *great city*, which *spiritually is called Sodom and* sym:sym-egypt[Egypt], *where also our Lord was crucified*.
____

One city, three names.
Where was the Lord crucified? — there is one answer, and every reader knows it.
And the verse says the other two names are what that city is called *spiritually* — the very kind of writing the woman carries on her forehead: __“MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF sym:sym-harlot[HARLOTS]”__ (Revelation 17:5) — a mystery-inscription; and in the seal's own grammar, the name on a forehead names the one she *belongs to*.

Nor did Revelation invent the method.
Isaiah stood in Jerusalem and addressed her rulers to their faces:

[quote.scripture, Isaiah 1:10]
____
Hear the word of the LORD, ye *rulers of Sodom*; give ear unto the law of our God, ye *people of Gomorrah*.
____

Ezekiel makes the kinship formal: __“thine elder sister is Samaria… and thy younger sister… is Sodom”__ (Ezekiel 16:46).
The prophets already called Jerusalem *Sodom* when she lived like Sodom.

sym:sym-egypt[Egypt] is the same grammar.
Egypt is __“the *house of bondage*”__ (Exodus 20:2) — and Paul writes of __“Jerusalem which now is,”__ that she __“is in *bondage* with her children”__ (Galatians 4:25): the covenant city living as the slave-house is called by the slave-house's name.
Ezekiel had already watched her earn it: Jerusalem the sym:sym-harlot[harlot] __“multiplied her sym:sym-fornication[whoredoms]”__ in remembering __“the days of her youth, wherein she had played the sym:sym-harlot[harlot] *in the land of Egypt*”__ (Ezekiel 23:19).

The last identifying mark is blood.
In the great city __“was found the *blood of prophets*, and of saints”__ (Revelation 18:24) — and Jesus fixed that address forever: __“upon you may come all the *righteous blood* shed upon the earth”__ (Matthew 23:35); __“it cannot be that a prophet perish *out of Jerusalem*”__ (Luke 13:33); __“O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that *killest the prophets*”__ (Matthew 23:37).
Sodom for her sin, Egypt for her bondage — and on her brow her owner's name, *Babylon*, the beast's mark — and the street where the witnesses lie dead runs through the city that crucified her King.
The unfaithful wife of the sym:sym-marriage[marriage] chapter and the boasting queen of the widows’ chapter are the same woman, and her *own* name is not a foreign capital's.

[discrete]
=== The Song on the Far Shore

The sea of glass scene now reads whole.
The victors stand where Israel stood — on the far side of the waters that drowned their pursuer — and they sing the same song, doubled: __“the song of Moses… and the song of the Lamb.”__
The first Exodus gave the pattern; the last performs it on every nation at once: plagues on the oppressor, a people called out, the pursuer sunk like a stone, and a shore with singing on it.
__“Thus shall Babylon sink, and shall not rise.”__
The sym:sym-gospel[gospel] the book has been reading all along ends exactly where it began at the Red Sea: the kingdom that would not let go, gone under the waters — and the people of God standing on glass, dry-shod, learning the old song by heart.

---
title: "Daniel Unsealed"
slug: daniel-unsealed
order: 36
permalink: /books/meat-bibles-symbolic-language/daniel-unsealed/
description: "Daniel was commanded to seal the book to the time of the end — and a seal implies an unsealing. Jeremiah's seventy years failed as a literal count (Babylon fell without a fight, the captives came home after sixty), and unpointed Daniel 9:24 opens with the same word twice — seventy seventy, seventy sevens of sevens: seventy jubilees. The ninth chapter's two decrees, 490 years apart from each rebuilding, and the twelfth chapter's past-tense 'the daily was taken away' with its 1,290 and 1,335 year-days, read straight through history — from the first decree to Messiah, from the second to the end of the times; the seal sits under the vowel points, and it opens with the fresh eyes the chapter “What Is the Point” argued for."
og_title: "Daniel Unsealed — MEAT The Bible's Symbolic Language"
epigraphs:
  - quote: "But thou, O Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end: many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall be increased."
    ref: "Daniel 12:4"
---
Daniel is the one prophet ordered to lock his own book.
__“Shut up the words, and sym:sym-seal[seal] the book, even to the time of the end”__ — and when he asks what his own visions mean, he is refused:

[quote.scripture, Daniel 12:9-10]
____
…Go thy way, Daniel: for the words are *closed up and sealed till the time of the end*… none of the wicked shall understand; but the sym:sym-wise[wise] shall sym:sym-understanding[understand].
____

A sealed book expects an unsealing.

A book sealed in Hebrew was never going to be unsealed by a translation of a translation: the vowel points are themselves the first translation, and our English Bibles translate the pointing, not the bare letters — so part of the seal sits in readings that first translation chose away.
This chapter takes the covering off with tools already forged — the chapter link:/books/symbolic-language/what-is-the-point/[_What Is the Point?_] made the case for revisiting these books with fresh eyes, the vowel points set aside — and unseals the way a seal demands: by translating again, this time from the letters themselves.

[discrete]
=== Seventy of What?

Start where Daniel himself started: with a promise of Jeremiah's that did not add up.

[quote.scripture, Jeremiah 25:11-12]
____
And this whole land shall be a desolation, and an astonishment; and these nations shall serve the king of sym:sym-babel[Babylon] seventy sym:sym-year[years].
And it shall come to pass, when seventy years are accomplished, that I will punish the king of Babylon, and that nation, saith the LORD, for their iniquity, and the land of the Chaldeans, and will make it *perpetual desolations*.
____

Many people, Daniel among them at first, understood this as Israel serving Babylon for seventy literal years.
But read carefully what the seventy must contain: all of Jeremiah's words brought upon that land — __“even all that is written in this book”__ (Jeremiah 25:13) — and Babylon made a desolation forever.

History did something else.
Babylon fell to Cyrus in 539 BC without a fight, during the Feast of Tabernacles, and was not made a perpetual desolation; the captives went home in 538 BC — some sixty years after Daniel was carried off, not seventy.
Either Jeremiah is a false prophet, or __“seventy years”__ counts seventy of some larger unit — for the word translated __“year”__ is a flexible measure of time, the way __“day”__ is.
Daniel had the same question:

[quote.scripture, Daniel 9:2]
____
In the first year of his reign I Daniel understood by books the number of the years, whereof the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet, that he would accomplish seventy sym:sym-year[years] in the desolations of Jerusalem.
____

He prays, and the angel Gabriel brings the answer:

[quote.scripture, Daniel 9:24 — the letters read again]
____
sym:sym-week[Weeks] seventy are *cut — divided, covenanted —* upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to *shut up* the transgression, and to *make an end of* sym:sym-sin[sins], and to *atone* for lawlessness, and to bring in everlasting sym:sym-righteousness[righteousness], and to *seal — complete — the vision and prophet*, and to anoint the most Holy.
____

Now set the verse side by side, word by word — the received points beside this book's, and beside every claimed sense its proof: the verse where the King James prints the same sense, or the repointed word itself.

<<<

.Daniel 9:24, word by word — the log, the two pointings, the prophecy
[.prevalence-table, frame=topbot, grid=none, cols="<26,>20,<26,<28", options="header"]
|===
| Log | Masorete | MEAT | Prophecy

| weeks | שָׁבֻעִים | _Deut 16:9 · H7620_ | Sevens — the jubilee count
| Seventy | שִׁבְעִים | | seventy
| are determined | נֶחְתַּךְ | _“to cut off” — H2852_ | is cut — divided, covenanted
| upon thy people | עַל־עַמְּךָ | | upon thy people
| and upon… city | וְעַל־עִיר | | and upon the city of
| thy holy | קָדְשֶׁךָ | | thy holiness
| to finish | לְכַלֵּא | _“refrained” — Ps 40:9 · H3607_ | to shut up
| the transgression | הַפֶּשַׁע | | the transgression
| and to make an end of | וּלְהָתֵם | | and to end
| sins | חַטָּאת | | sins
| and to make reconciliation | וּלְכַפֵּר | _“pitch” — Gen 6:14 · H3722_ | and to atone
| for iniquity | עָוֹן | | for lawlessness
| and to bring in | וּלְהָבִיא | | and to bring in
| righteousness | צֶדֶק | | righteousness
| everlasting | עֹלָמִים | | of the ages
| and to seal up | וְלַחְתֹּם | _“seal the book” — Dan 12:4 · H2856_ | and to seal — complete
| the vision | חָזוֹן | | the vision
| and prophecy | וְנָבִיא | _“prophet” — H5030_ | and prophet
| and to anoint | וְלִמְשֹׁחַ | _H4886_ | and to anoint
| the most Holy | קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים | _the doubling again — Isa 26:3_ | the holy of holies
|===

The goals themselves are jubilee-work.
The transgression is shut up while the jubilee opens the prison — __“the opening of the prison to them that are bound”__ (Isaiah 61:1); sins end as a slave's service ends — __“whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin”__ (John 8:34), and at the jubilee the servant __“shall return unto his own family”__ (Leviticus 25:41).
The atonement is the jubilee's own gate — the trumpet of the fiftieth year sounds __“in the day of atonement”__ (Leviticus 25:9) — and its economics, the kinsman buying back what was sold.
Righteousness of the ages is every man restored __“unto the possession of his fathers”__ (Leviticus 25:41), and the count closes on an anointing, because proclaiming the Jubilee is the Anointed One's own commission: __“the LORD hath *anointed* me… to proclaim *liberty* to the captives”__ (Isaiah 61:1).
A count measured in jubilees, given to do jubilee-work.

Sins have not been ended, and the vision of Jeremiah has not been completed — so seventy __“weeks,”__ four hundred ninety years, cannot be the whole of it.
Look at the letters.
The Hebrew under __“weeks”__ is the seven-word in a plural form — and with the points removed, the verse opens with the same word written twice:

[.text-center.breath]
שבעים שבעים — *seventy seventy*

[.breath]
The plural ending makes the seven at least double — and a complete cycle of sevens, seven sevens, is the jubilee.
Jeremiah's unit was already compared to a year, and a year is itself a complete cycle of time; so the letters give us seventy sevens-of-sevens: *seventy jubilees* — seventy times 49 years — 3,430 in all.footnote:jubilee[The count runs from Israel crossing the Jordan — the year the jubilee clock started — with the date and the counting conventions (no year zero; a year is the space between the marks, not the marks) established in my chronology study, _Time Tested Tradition_.]
The jubilee clock started at the Jordan crossing in 1406 BC, and the seventieth jubilee year closed in the spring of 2026.

That places 2026-2027 in the *third year* of Hezekiah's sign — two fallow years, __“and in the third year *sow ye, and reap*”__ (Isaiah 37:30) — and the third is the year of going up: __“on the *third day* thou shalt *go up unto the house of the LORD*”__ (2 Kings 20:5).
The letters also permit a second reading, and both can stand: seventy seventy as seventy times seventy — 4,900 years __“determined upon *thy people*,”__ the seed of Abraham.
That count runs from the covenant itself, sealed in 1876 BC, 430 years to the selfsame day before the Exodus (Exodus 12:40-41) — and if the reign of a thousand years is its final millennium, the reign opens 3,900 years in: the very year the seventieth jubilee closed.
The count's own first verb names its starting line: _nechtak_ — cut, divided — the word of the covenant of the pieces, __“divided… in the midst”__ as the lamp __“passed between those pieces”__ (Genesis 15:10, 17).
Two counts, two starting lines four centuries apart — and they close on the same year.

[discrete]
=== The Count at Two Scales

The Torah has already run this very count at two scales.
The word under Daniel's __“weeks”__ is the name of a feast — _Shavuot_, the Feast of sym:sym-week[Weeks], the Feast of Sevens — and that feast is counted exactly the way the jubilee is counted: __“seven sabbaths shall be complete: even unto the morrow after the seventh sabbath shall ye number *fifty days*”__ (Leviticus 23:15-16), as the jubilee numbers __“seven sabbaths of sym:sym-year[years]”__ and hallows __“the *fiftieth year*”__ (Leviticus 25:8, 10).
Seven sevens of days to a fiftieth day; seven sevens of years to a fiftieth year.

The Feast of Weeks is the jubilee run in days — the Torah's own day-for-a-year model, rehearsed every spring on the way to Pentecost.
So when Gabriel answers a question about years in *sevens*, the scale is already licensed: the count that walks in days walks in years.

Daniel marks his own scales.
One chapter later, mourning three ordinary weeks, he writes __“three sevens *of days*”__ (Daniel 10:2-3) — the King James prints __“three *full* weeks”__ — the numeral leading and the scale named, exactly as the feast counts: __“*seven* weeks shalt thou number”__ (Deuteronomy 16:9).
This prophecy inverts that order — *Sevens seven… Sevens sixty-and-two* — the noun leading its own count, and no scale named anywhere: the bare Sevens are not day-weeks and not year-weeks; they are the feast's unit, the jubilee's shape.
The hint survives the pointing itself: the Masoretes kept the Sevens first even as they pointed “weeks” — the received text preserves, on its own grammar, the mark that these are no calendar weeks, which means its keepers knew something was here; only the King James's “Seventy weeks,” smoothing the order for English, hid the signal.

The letters go one step further.
Written without points, the plural here is letter for letter the number *seventy* — the spelling Scripture uses some ninety times — and the pointing that reads “weeks” appears only in this prophecy; the vowels decide, and context chooses the vowels.
Scripture's own idiom crowns the choice: a doubled word is the thing perfected — _shalom shalom_ the King James prints __“*perfect* peace”__ (Isaiah 26:3); _tzedek tzedek_, __“*altogether* just”__ (Deuteronomy 16:20) — and this verse is framed in doublings: the Sevens perfected at its head, and __“the *most Holy*”__ — the holy of holies — perfected at its close.
The doubling also multiplies: when Jesus set the measure of forgiveness He reached for this figure — __“until *seventy times seven*”__ (Matthew 18:22) — the Greek hearing the pair multiplied, 490, the count of the very prophecy given to make an end of sins; the Hebrew Matthew hears __“seventy and seven,”__ Lamech's vengeance-count (Genesis 4:24) answered in forgiveness.
One skeleton, every arithmetic the letters allow — and the fiftieth that crowns each seven-of-sevens carries the same cargo at every scale: __“proclaim *liberty* throughout all the land”__ (Leviticus 25:10) in the fiftieth year; the Spirit poured out on the fiftieth day, and __“where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is *liberty*”__ (2 Corinthians 3:17).

[discrete]
=== The Two Decrees

Gabriel then divides the count from a landmark anyone can check:

[quote.scripture, Daniel 9:25]
____
Know therefore and understand, that from the going forth of the commandment to *restore and to build Jerusalem* unto the *Messiah the Prince* shall be seven sym:sym-week[weeks], and threescore and two weeks: the street shall be built again, and the wall, even in troublous times.
____

The __“weeks”__ here carry the same plural form as verse 24 — and the word the King James renders __“two”__ is also the Hebrew for *second, another*; the word for __“seventy”__ can stand for the jubilee-cycle it completes.
Read the letters again:

[quote.scripture, Daniel 9:25 — the letters read again]
____
Know therefore and understand, that from the going forth of the word to restore and build Jerusalem until Messiah the Prince shall be *seventy seven* [490 years] — then *Jubilee sixty, and another* [490]: they will come back and build again, with the *plaza and the moat* — and in distress [shall be] the times.
____

<<<
